item.title: Where is it going wrong for Carrick's Man Utd?
item.description: Thursday marks five months exactly since Man Utd announced Michael Carrick would be staying on as head coach. There will be little mood for celebrating anniversaries the morning after his worst night in the role.

item.title: Today's 5️⃣: Madrid run riot, Betis win and Boca learn their opponents
item.description: Today's 5️⃣: Madrid run riot, Betis win and Boca learn their opponents Good morning, football fans. The third round of Champions League matches wrapped up yesterday, and there’s plenty to talk about at home and abroad. Here are the day’s top 5 stories. Let’s get started. Real Madrid cruise to emphatic win over Leipzig Los Blancos enjoyed a brilliant night in Europe with a convincing victory over RB Leipzig. They controlled the game from the opening whistle and were ruthlessly effective in attack. The tactical game plan worked to perfection on the pitch. Their high press repeatedly forced the German side to give the ball away, allowing the home attackers to pose a constant threat. 📸 Diego Souto - 2026 Getty Images The win gives Real Madrid a confidence boost heading into El Clásico next Sunday, October 25. Betis beat Feyenoord and keep making history Betis still have a perfect record in the Champions League. Manuel Pellegrini ’s men edged past Feyenoord thanks to an Isco penalty and continue to dream big. 📸 JORGE GUERRERO - AFP or licensors The road ahead is tough, but not impossible: Dortmund, Slovan Bratislava, Como, Arsenal and Bayern. The build-up to El Clásico heats up This Sunday’s El Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou will have plenty of talking points, including José Mourinho’s return to Barcelona. The clash between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid will also be marked by tensions between the clubs’ leadership: Florentino Pérez will not travel to Barcelona, so there will be no reunion with Joan Laporta. 📸 Angel Martinez - 2025 Getty Images Real Sociedad and Celta de Vigo prepare for European action A demanding day awaits Spain’s representatives in Europe. Real Sociedad and Celta de Vigo are putting the finishing touches to their preparations for this afternoon’s UEFA Europa League fixtures. Both teams are chasing their first win in the competition: Matarazzo’s side have one point, while Claudio Giráldez’s men have none. Atlético Mineiro reach Sudamericana final; Palmeiras reach Libertadores final The finalists in South America’s two continental competitions are taking shape. Atlético Mineiro booked their place in the Copa Sudamericana final after edging past Montevideo City Torque 3-2 on aggregate. The final is now confirmed: Boca Juniors vs Atlético Mineiro in Barranquilla. 📸 Ernesto Ryan - 2026 Getty Images Meanwhile, the Copa Libertadores clash between Palmeiras and Fluminense went down to the wire, with the Verdão securing their place in the final in a penalty shootout. Palmeiras await the winner of today’s meeting between Flamengo and Estudiantes. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Leam Richardson Praises Reading’s Defence In 1-0 Leyton Orient Win
item.description: The Royals secured a brilliant 1-0 victory over Leyton Orient at the SCL Stadium to move into the League One play-off places. A second-half strike from Paddy Lane proved to be the difference, although the Royals could have enjoyed a more comfortable victory after Lewis Wing saw his first-half penalty saved. The victory moves Reading up to sixth in the table. Royals boss Leam Richardson spoke to Royals TV to share his thoughts on the performance and another important three points. Richardson on the victory “Yeah, a good response from the weekend. The result, not the performance, but yeah, clean sheets – I love clean sheets! “I thought we worked hard, certainly in the second half. We started the game really well. I thought we were really good with the ball and without the ball, and caused them all sorts of problems. “I think they changed shape a couple of times as well, which is always a good sign of respect. We’re probably disappointed not to go in at half-time one or two goals up. “In the second half, we had to be really good without the ball. Although it looked like they had some good shots, I don’t really remember Joel having to make any massive saves. “I thought we were quite comfortable controlling the ball. We probably started to play the result a little bit for 20 minutes, but that’s human nature. We’re at home and we’re trying everything we can to win. “We made changes to get us back up the pitch a little bit, and the lads who came on did their jobs really well. “The goal was a typical team goal. Our possession, controlling the spaces where we wanted to be, and then in transition, it was fantastic. A really good team goal, so I’m really pleased.” Richardson on Lewis Wing’s missed penalty “Listen, we’ve got good players. We knew there was nothing lost, nothing gained. We’ve got to stay strong with it. “He’s very experienced, Wingy, isn’t he? So I’ve got no issues with that. He’ll take the next one. “He’s disappointed like everybody else, but I thought him and Andy in the middle of the pitch were excellent tonight, with and without the ball. “In the first half, they were fantastic. They made great decisions, changing play, and then I thought without the ball in the second half, the lads were really controlled. “The wide players on the outside, the nine and the 10 in front of them, I thought we were very good.” Richardson on the defensive performance and clean sheet “It’s not just about the back four and the goalkeeper, you need all 11. “You see how hard the lads work for 60 or 70 minutes, controlling where we wanted to put the ball for large parts of the game. I think it’s credit to everybody, all the way through to Joel. “We were very methodical in what we were doing without the ball in the last 20 minutes, so that was really pleasing. “I think we probably deserved the win off the back of our endeavour without the ball in the second half and the way we played in the first half.” Richardson the fans “I’ve got to say, towards the end, I felt

I was trying to make changes, but I thought the fans played a massive part. A massive part. “They put energy onto the pitch. You could see it. They brought the lads to life. “I thought collectively, from the staff to the players to the fans, it was a big win tonight.” Richardson on moving into the play-off places “Listen, of course it’s important. item.title: “It will be so sad” - MotoGP riders lament loss of Phillip Island
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP riders have voiced their disappointment at Phillip Island’s impending departure from the championship, with many describing it as one of their favourite venues on the calendar. This weekend’s Australian Grand Prix marks MotoGP’s final visit to Phillip Island, with the series set to move to a revamped Adelaide street circuit next year. The 4.4km circuit has proved extremely popular with the grid, who have been won over by its high-speed layout, frequent elevation changes and old-school characteristics. The atmosphere at the venue located south of Melbourne adds to the appeal of the race, with its coastal setting and scenic views making it a distinctive stop on the MotoGP calendar. As the only Australian on the grid, Pramac’s Jack Miller showered praise on the Phillip Island Circuit and explained what makes the track so special for him. “[The emotions are] pretty high,” he said. “It’s probably one of the most iconic tracks on the calendar and produced arguably some of the best races we've ever seen in MotoGP. “Phillip Island is a track where if you haven't got the bike working amazing, you can still make up a bit of difference once you get the thing round up. Our bike turns pretty good. So as long as we can kind of get it round up and get it turning all right, you should be in with a shout. “This place is phenomenal, and on a MotoGP bike riding around here, it's something particular. You're kind of dancing with the bike the whole way through, trying to manage the shaking, the wheelie and the way the bike deals with the wind. “You can never fully attack. You're kind of just playing with the bike the whole time, which makes it all the more fun to ride. “I thought as ironic as it gets, we'd have fantastic weather throughout the weekend after what we've had the last couple of years with some trying conditions. But it doesn't look that way. Phillip Island is giving itself a proper send-off with some ever-changing conditions.” KTM’s Pedro Acosta said he puts Phillip Island in the same breath as legendary motorcycle tracks like Mugello, as he prepares to bid farewell to the venue. Asked how riders would feel on their last visit to Melbourne, Acosta said: “On one side, it will be beautiful for everyone; and on the other one, it will be so sad. “One of the best atmospheres around the whole calendar, the fans are so close to us. Also, the track is one of these legendary tracks around the championship, like Mugello, Jerez and other ones around. “It will be so sad that next year we don't come here.” Phillip Island track details Phillip Island track details Marc Marquez , a two-time winner of the Australian Grand Prix, described Phillip Island is a track that commands respect from riders. “It’s one of my favourites and I really enjoy it,” he said. “But it’s a very fast, very narrow track, where if you crash, you’re in the gravel in no time. “It’s one of those tracks that riders have a healthy respect for; it’s a bit like Holland too – yo
item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo MotoGP riders have voiced their disappointment at Phillip Island’s impending departure from the championship, with many describing it as one of their favourite venues on the calendar. This weekend’s Australian Grand Prix marks MotoGP’s final visit to Phillip Island, with the series set to move to a revamped Adelaide street circuit next year. The 4.4km circuit has proved extremely popular with the grid, who have been won over by its high-speed layout, frequent elevation changes and old-school characteristics. The atmosphere at the venue located south of Melbourne adds to the appeal of the race, with its coastal setting and scenic views making it a distinctive stop on the MotoGP calendar. As the only Australian on the grid, Pramac’s Jack Miller showered praise on the Phillip Island Circuit and explained what makes the track so special for him. “[The emotions are] pretty high,” he said. “It’s probably one of the most iconic tracks on the calendar and produced arguably some of the best races we've ever seen in MotoGP. “Phillip Island is a track where if you haven't got the bike working amazing, you can still make up a bit of difference once you get the thing round up. Our bike turns pretty good. So as long as we can kind of get it round up and get it turning all right, you should be in with a shout. “This place is phenomenal, and on a MotoGP bike riding around here, it's something particular. You're kind of dancing with the bike the whole way through, trying to manage the shaking, the wheelie and the way the bike deals with the wind. “You can never fully attack. You're kind of just playing with the bike the whole time, which makes it all the more fun to ride. “I thought as ironic as it gets, we'd have fantastic weather throughout the weekend after what we've had the last couple of years with some trying conditions. But it doesn't look that way. Phillip Island is giving itself a proper send-off with some ever-changing conditions.” KTM’s Pedro Acosta said he puts Phillip Island in the same breath as legendary motorcycle tracks like Mugello, as he prepares to bid farewell to the venue. Asked how riders would feel on their last visit to Melbourne, Acosta said: “On one side, it will be beautiful for everyone; and on the other one, it will be so sad. “One of the best atmospheres around the whole calendar, the fans are so close to us. Also, the track is one of these legendary tracks around the championship, like Mugello, Jerez and other ones around. “It will be so sad that next year we don't come here.” Phillip Island track details Phillip Island track details Marc Marquez , a two-time winner of the Australian Grand Prix, described Phillip Island is a track that commands respect from riders. “It’s one of my favourites and I really enjoy it,” he said. “But it’s a very fast, very narrow track, where if you crash, you’re in the gravel in no time. “It’s one of those tracks that riders have a healthy respect for; it’s a bit like Holland too – you’ve got that respect for it. “The final section is the one that really impresses, especially on the first few laps, and it’ll continue to impress this year.” Marquez’s title rival Jorge Martin also highlighted the appeal of the wider Phillip Island experience, where riders often stay in rented holiday homes rather than conventional hotels. “I'm sure I will miss Phillip Island for the next few years. Maybe we will come back in the future, but for the moment I will miss it,” he said. “First of all, the track itself. It's nice to ride here. It's really different from what we are used to. It's really fast. You need to put a lot of technique to be fast here. Since I arrived here in Moto3, I always loved it. “Then, the place. The vibe here is great. Also, you're in a house with all this wildlife where you can surf and everything. So it's a nice place and I always enjoyed it.” While Phillip Island has a cult following within motorcycle racing, ageing facilities and limited accommodation options had cast doubt over its future for several years. This year, the state government of South Australia secured a new deal to move MotoGP away from Victoria, with the Adelaide street circuit that once staged Formula 1 races gearing up to host the premier class next year. While MotoGP riders have softened their stance on Adelaide after MotoGP allayed their safety concerns with an AI-generated onboard video, they admit they will miss the outgoing Phillip Island. Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing “Phillip Island was always a beautiful race for the show, for the TV and for the fans,” said Honda rider Luca Marini . “In some years, it was maybe the most beautiful race of the year. 2018, 2017, I don't remember well, but the races were unbelievable, and also later on. “It's always the [winners’] trophy; it's unbelievable. It's something that I always dream about, but unfortunately, I was not on the podium here, so let's try in the wet this year. “It will be another amazing trophy because I think it's still one piece with history, with a unique style that you can find. You can win only here, and for the riders, the trophy is always important.” Aprilia star Marco Bezzecchi added: “Normally, at beautiful tracks, you always have very beautiful races. Here the battles have always been amazing. “Last year, the race was fantastic. It was my first MotoGP podium [in Phillip Island] as well. So, it was good.” Phillip Island first hosted the Australian GP in 1989 and became a permanent fixture on the calendar in 1997, replacing Eastern Creek. This year will mark the 30th and final world championship race on the island. item.title: Courtois sends warning to Barcelona as Real Madrid prepare for El Clasico
item.description: Courtois sends warning to Barcelona as Real Madrid prepare for El Clasico Real Madrid kept up their perfect record in this UEFA Champions League campaign as they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in their third League Phase game. Several players stood out for the Merengue side in this game, but despite the margin with which they won, it was not really an easy game. One of these players who impressed in this game was the goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, as he had to make several interventions, especially in the first half, to keep the visitors from scoring. However, he was still unable to keep a clean sheet as the Germans scored one goal in the second half. As MARCA has reported, the Belgian veteran also talked to the media after the game. He was quite confident for the upcoming game against Barcelona, especially after the team’s recent good run of form: “I think we’ve played some good matches, picked up some good wins and made a great comeback in Rome. We’re confident about what lies ahead, and we know it’s going to be a tough match. But if we want to close the gap in the league, we’ll have to go there and win.” “You never know until you actually play the match. I think we’re in a good place and full of confidence. They’ve been doing very well in the league, but I believe in our team and think we can go there and win. It’s true that we’re playing away from home, and that makes a difference, but I believe in our team. For me, Clásicos are always 50-50, even when one team comes into the match in better form than the other.” The Real Madrid captain put his support behind Vinicius Junior after another underwhelming performance from the Brazilian: “No, I think he’s looking to get back to his best, and I’m sure he’ll get there with the support of the team and the fans. I think he played well. I saw him making dangerous runs and creating threats, but things don’t always go your way. “There are only two players I know of who have been at their best almost every season: Cristiano and Messi. I’ve watched them perform at that level year after year, and even two of the greatest players in history have been criticised at various points. That’s football. I think Vinícius has been playing almost every game for nine years, so we have to help him get back to his best. But he’s the first to be happy, enjoy himself and work towards reaching his best level.” While admitting that Real Madrid have struggled away from home, the goalie also pointed to the team’s improving form ahead of a stretch of away games: “Home and away matches are always different, and we’ve found it more difficult to get results away from home, in places like Spain, Rome and Elche, followed by the two defeats against Betis. I think we deserved more against Betis. We lost, but we played well. “It’s true that we need to improve away from home, but I think we’re doing well now that we’re back after the international break. We’ll be eager for Sunday and for what lies ahead, because we have four away matches coming up, and if we don’t want to lose touch in the league, these next three matches are crucial.” Taking a different line from his manager and the club, Courtois put his trust in referees ahead of the match against Barcelona: “No, because I trust the referees. I believe they go into matches intending to do the best they can, and they’re human beings who can make mistakes. However, we hope those mistakes aren’t always made in favour of one side rather than the other. “When VAR intervenes, we hope it’s for the kinds of incidents it was introduced to deal with. But I’m an optimistic person, and I want to believe that referees always go onto the pitch with honest intentions. As I said, they can make mistakes, which is why VAR exists. That’s all.” Thibaut Courtois will once again have to be at his best as Real Madrid are set to face one of the strongest teams in Europe this Sunday. Hopefully, he will be able to keep a clean sheet in that game, and help the Merengues get a win over their bitter rivals.

item.title: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a productive offseason, Yaxel Lendeborg made his debut for the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday. His first task? Try to stop Luka Doncic. It was an unenviable assignment for the rookie forward. But it was also a good test. Unfortunately for Lendeborg, he did not study enough, and Doncic made him pay for it . The Los Angeles Lakers blew out the Warriors, 127-105, at Crypto.com Arena. Lendeborg had 12 points, three rebounds, and two assists in 29 minutes. He was whistled for a technical foul for talking trash to Luka Doncic in the second quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the postgame interview, coach Steve Kerr pointed out the 24-year-old Lendeborg’s learning curve . “This was a great welcome-to-the-NBA game for him. Having to guard Luka, who is as tough to guard as anybody in the world. Having to learn all the little tricks that exist in the NBA. He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff,” said Kerr in the video posted by The Athletic’s Anthony Slater. “It’s his first game. He’s an unbelievable young guy, great talent. It was a frustrating night for him, but a lesson well learned, and he’ll get better from here.” Steve Kerr on Yaxel Lendeborg guarding Luka Doncic in his debut: “He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff.” Kerr didn’t like the technical on Yaxel and not Luka also: “Kind of ridiculous.” pic.twitter.com/SM87XvVY9Y — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 22, 2026 Kerr, who has steered the Warriors to four titles, added that guarding Doncic was “not an easy way to start your career,” although he claimed that the six-time All-NBA got off easily during his verbal spat with Lendeborg. “He (Doncic) kind of lured him (Lendeborg) in a little bit. I thought the single technical was kind of ridiculous. They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel chose that got him the T, but then Luka made a half-court shot and got in his face. That should be a tech. Should’ve been a double tech. That feels good, the rookie treatment,” said Kerr with a chuckle. The Warriors will battle the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the postgame interview, coach Steve Kerr pointed out the 24-year-old Lendeborg’s learning curve . “This was a great welcome-to-the-NBA game for him. Having to guard Luka, who is as tough to guard as anybody in the world. Having to learn all the little tricks that exist in the NBA. He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff,” said Kerr in the video posted by The Athletic’s Anthony Slater. “It’s his first game. He’s an unbelievable young guy, great talent. It was a frustrating night for him, but a lesson well learned, and he’ll get better from here.” Steve Kerr on Yaxel Lendeborg guarding Luka Doncic in his debut: “He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff.” Kerr didn’t like the technical on Yaxel and not Luka also: “Kind of ridiculous.” pic.twitter.com/SM87XvVY9Y — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 22, 2026 Kerr, who has steered the Warriors to four titles, added that guarding Doncic was “not an easy way to start your career,” although he claimed that the six-time All-NBA got off easily during his verbal spat with Lendeborg. “He (Doncic) kind of lured him (Lendeborg) in a little bit. I thought the single technical was kind of ridiculous. They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel chose that got him the T, but then Luka made a half-court shot and got in his face. That should be a tech. Should’ve been a double tech. That feels good, the rookie treatment,” said Kerr with a chuckle. The Warriors will battle the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: Jamie Carragher tears into ‘disgraceful’ Bruno Fernandes over Man United captain’s Como outburst
item.description: Jamie Carragher has labelled Bruno Fernandes ’ comments on Michael Carrick ’s tactics as “disgraceful” after Manchester United descended into crisis after a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. Cesc Fabregas’ side swept past Carrick’s United with Fernandes visibly upset on the pitch before an outburst at his side’s inability to press. “It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them,” Fernandes said. “But sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.” Th 32-year-old then made a pointed remark that United should have “more brave under pressure,” with the heavy defeat now leaving them 20th in the table after three rounds of fixtures in the league phase and seven games without a win in all competitions. “For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it's a disgrace,” Carragher said on CBS Sports . “When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. Bruno Fernandes claimed United should have been braver against Como (Reuters) “Carrick put him back in his rightful position. And he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. “But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent. But in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all. And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off. “When he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. “I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it.”

item.title: How Houston Rockets implemented preseason talking points to great success in opening night romp
item.description: Kevin Durant and the Rockets had 29 fast-break points in Wednesday's season-opening win over the Mavericks as Fred VanVleet's return helped unlock a faster-paced offense. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The two generals, one on the court and the other on the field, faced each other, with one readying for the other's verdict. The former, Fred VanVleet, had just hurled an off-balance pass from his own 3-point line to the opposite end of the court - hitting Kevin Durant in stride for an open dunk. Houston 's point guard turned to his right where the city's quarterback, C.J. Stroud , sat courtside. VanVleet - tilting his hand from side to side - wanted a rating. Stroud gave him two thumbs up. "That's my guy. I don't expect anything less," VanVleet said after the Rockets' 128-110 win at Toyota Center . "I would have been hurt if he would have (given) me a thumbs down." The bucket counted for two of the Rockets' 29 fast-break points - tying their second-highest total from last season, early proof of the faster pace coach Ime Udoka has emphasized through training camp. The Rockets were the second-slowest team in the league last season, forcing them to attack set defenses and often leading to contested shots as the shot clock dwindled. But Wednesday's season opener looked different. Houston shot 52.2% from the field, 44.4% from 3-point range and had assists on 32 of their 47 made baskets. It's just one game against a bad team, but VanVleet's return, offseason additions and a change in tempo gave the Rockets offense some much-needed WD-40 to smoothen the offense. "The ball respects energy and it's contagious," VanVleet said. "So when it's moving and guys are moving and flowing, the shots get better quality and the shots tend to go in more." Playing faster isn't a costless endeavor. Udoka pointed to turnovers and some poor early shot selection as potential tradeoffs. But the Rockets, with VanVleet back on the court and helping limit giveaways, feel they can live with those issues because of the advantages faster pace gets them. Going against a scrambling defense can lead to easy buckets or mismatches as defenders mark whoever is in front of them. Durant and center Alperen Sengun both profited off those "cross-matches." (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The two generals, one on the court and the other on the field, faced each other, with one readying for the other's verdict. The former, Fred VanVleet, had just hurled an off-balance pass from his own 3-point line to the opposite end of the court - hitting Kevin Durant in stride for an open dunk. But Wednesday's season opener looked different. Houston shot 52.2% from the field, 44.4% from 3-point range and had assists on 32 of their 47 made baskets. "The ball respects energy and it's contagious," VanVleet said. "So when it's moving and guys are moving and flowing, the shots get better quality and the shots tend to go in more." Playing faster isn't a costless endeavor. Udoka pointed to turnovers and some poor early shot selection as potential tradeoffs. But the Rockets, with VanVleet back on the court and helping limit giveaways, feel they can live with those issues because of the advantages faster pace gets them. Going against a scrambling defense can lead to easy buckets or mismatches as defenders mark whoever is in front of them. Durant and center Alperen Sengun both profited off those "cross-matches." Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) puts up a shot around Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington (25) during the first half at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Houston fueled much of that transition attack with another stylistic shift: Aggressive off-ball defense forcing turnovers. Rather than stay on their assignments, especially when guarding below-average shooters, Rockets defenders would move to the middle of the floor to clog driving and passing lanes. Udoka talked about forcing turnovers as a way to "squeeze" more out of an already-elite defense that allowed the fourth-fewest points per 100 possessions last season, per Cleaning the Glass. The Rockets forced turnovers at a bottom-10 rate last season. On Wednesday, the Mavericks committed 21 giveaways that led to 32 Houston points. Houston also entered the season wanting to take more 3-pointers after doing so at one of the lowest rates in the league last season. The Rockets took 36 on Thursday, not an elite mark but still higher than last season's average. The additional shooting opens up opportunities inside. "Last year we started in our backcourt, Twin (Amen Thompson) and Josh Okogie. And a lot of times those guys (were) being left (open) at the 3-point line," Durant said. " … When we got Fred and Marcus Smart out there, who can keep the defense honest at the 3-point line and then twin just roaming around just doing everything … that (puts) everybody in a good position. I think that settled everybody into what they do best." It isn't just about having more shooters. It's also about where they lurk. Jabari Smith Jr., who made four 3-pointers and tied Durant for the team high with 30 points, pointed to Houston's improved off-ball movement, a focus during training camp. The goal, Smith Jr. said, is to keep the defense moving as much as possible. The Rockets were able to implement that change and others to great success in the opener. Now, Houston's goal shifts to maintaining those growth areas moving forward, especially with an imposing test against Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs looming on Friday in Austin. item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic isn’t just settling into life with the Los Angeles Lakers ; he is fully embracing the spotlight as the new face of the iconic franchise. Following a dominant 127-105 season-opening victory over the Golden State Warriors, the Slovenian superstar reflected on what it means to carry the mantle for one of the most storied brands in professional sports. Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg tried poking the bear with some second-quarter chatter, but Doncic quickly turned the noise into motivation. He took over the game, pouring in 23 of his 28 points in the first half to put the contest out of reach early. By the end of the night, Doncic stuffed the box score with 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and three steals in just 30 minutes of action. He was efficient from distance as well, drilling five 3-pointers and dictating the tempo from start to finish. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When asked after the game about carrying the weight of the franchise on his shoulders and his long-term future in Southern California, Doncic kept it real about how much the opportunity means to him. “Obviously it’s the Lakers, it’s one of the biggest organizations in the world, if not the biggest,” Doncic said. “It’s a lot of honor just to be the face of this franchise. I hope I can stay here long. It doesn’t feel different, but like I said, it’s very much an honor, and I’m just enjoying this moment.” Luka on being the face of the Lakers: "Obviously it's the Lakers, it's one of the biggest organizations in the world, if not the biggest. It's a lot of honor just to be the face of this franchise. I hope I can stay here long. It doesn't feel different, but like I said, it's very… pic.twitter.com/rkZvhqqRJS — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 22, 2026 Doncic showed no signs of feeling pressure on opening night. Instead, he delivered the kind of commanding performance that defines elite franchise pillars. If Wednesday’s masterpiece against Golden State was a glimpse of what is to come, purple and gold faithful can rest easy knowing the future of the organization is in capable hands. Doncic is not merely occupying the throne in Los Angeles, he plans on keeping it for a long time. Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: Celtic v Celta Vigo – This is a must win match for both sides
item.description: Celtic v Celta Vigo – This is a must win match for both sides Tonight is a must win match for both teams so we can expect an open and exciting contest. A draw is pretty much useless for both teams as both need the three points to kickstart their campaign… Callum Osmand of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Some Celtic supporters see the Europa League as a mere distraction, especially with our main rivals for the title spared the distraction of European football, but it’s still a tournament we should aspire to compete in. Tonight’s opponents are La Liga side Celta Vigo who visit Paradise for the first time on competitive business in nearly quarter of a century, and it will be a tough assignment to earn all three points. Benjamin Nygren of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026 . (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) After losing our first two fixtures and conceding seven goals in the process, it’s vital we kickstart our Europa campaign by snatching a victory, which will not only help our hopes of advancing, it will also give us some much needed confidence in our own ability in regards to competing at this level. Celta will also be of similar thinking as much like Celtic they have also lost their opening two fixtures, and will naturally be looking for a positive result. Kieran Tierney of Celtic celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) There’s also the financial benefit on offer, with £385,000 available for winning all three points, and although not a fortune it’s still a handsome bonus all the same. But the main focus will be to get back to winning ways on the European front, and try to win back some of our dented pride after two disjointed and disappointing performances and terrible results. Celta of course played at Celtic Park back in 2002 during Martin O’Neill’s star studded sides run to Seville, and won 1-0 courtesy of a Henrik Larsson goal which gave the Hoops a slender win to take to Spain. John Hartson of Celtic celebrates scoring during the UEFA Cup, 3rd Round, 2nd leg game between Celta Vigo and Celtic held on December 12, 2002 at the Campo De Futbol De Balaidos in Vigo, Spain. Celta Vigo won the match 2-1, Celtic won the tie 2-2 on away goals. (Photo by Laurence Griffiths/Getty Images) Celtic would unfortunately lose 2-1 in Spain, but would advance on away goals thanks to a John Hartson strike. A repeat of the Celtic Park scoreline would be most welcome tonight as we look to get our first Europa league points on the board. item.title: Arda Guler jokes about stealing Mbappe’s goal after Real Madrid beat Leipzig: ‘I knew he’d score another’
item.description: Arda Guler jokes about stealing Mbappe’s goal after Real Madrid beat Leipzig: ‘I knew he’d score another’ Arda Guler has revealed why he took the opportunity to score Real Madrid’s second goal in their 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig , joking that Kylian Mbappe would find the net again anyway. The Turkish midfielder was among Real Madrid’s standout contributors on matchday three and praised his team’s performance both in possession and without the ball. With the European fixture behind them, Guler also made clear that Real Madrid are already focused on the challenge of facing Barcelona in El Clasico. Guler praises Real Madrid’s performance against Leipzig Madrid’s victory provided another positive result in their Champions League campaign, with Guler pleased by the team’s work across both phases of the game. Speaking to Real Madrid TV after the final whistle, the midfielder stressed that the performance was about more than the goals scored. Arda Guler joked about Kylian Mbappe’s goal. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “We’re really pleased because I think we played brilliantly, both with and without the ball. I think we put in a great performance and we’re very happy,” he began. Guler also explained the expectations that come with representing the Spanish giants, insisting that winning must remain the standard regardless of the opponent or competition. “This is what we have to do. We’re Real Madrid, and we have to win every match.” Guler jokes about taking Mbappe’s goal One of the lighter moments from Guler’s interview came when he discussed his goal against Leipzig. The midfielder acknowledged that he had taken the opportunity away from Mbappe, but suggested there was little reason for concern given the French forward’s scoring ability. Arda Guler was crucial for Real Madrid in the Leipzig win. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “I stole the goal from Mbappe, but that’s because I knew he’d score another one. So, no problem.” The young Turk also pointed to the influence of playing at the Santiago Bernabeu, where the home crowd provides an additional motivation for the team. “It’s a key factor because when we play at home, in front of our fans, we try to give it our all for them.” Attention now turns to Sunday’s El Clasico , with Guler recognising the importance of the meeting and promising that Madrid will be ready to compete for the victory. “It’s a big match, a top-class fixture, and we’ll give it our all to win. We’re ready,” he concluded.

The Turkish midfielder was among Real Madrid’s standout contributors on matchday three and praised his team’s performance both in possession and without the ball. With the European fixture behind them, Guler also made clear that Real Madrid are already focused on the challenge of facing Barcelona in El Clasico. Guler praises Real Madrid’s performance against Leipzig Madrid’s victory provided another positive result in their Champions League campaign, with Guler pleased by the team’s work across both phases of the game. Speaking to Real Madrid TV after the final whistle, the midfielder stressed that the performance was about more than the goals scored. Arda Guler joked about Kylian Mbappe’s goal. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “We’re really pleased because I think we played brilliantly, both with and without the ball. I think we put in a great performance and we’re very happy,” he began. Guler also explained the expectations that come with representing the Spanish giants, insisting that winning must remain the standard regardless of the opponent or competition. “This is what we have to do. We’re Real Madrid, and we have to win every match.” Guler jokes about taking Mbappe’s goal One of the lighter moments from Guler’s interview came when he discussed his goal against Leipzig. The midfielder acknowledged that he had taken the opportunity away from Mbappe, but suggested there was little reason for concern given the French forward’s scoring ability. Arda Guler was crucial for Real Madrid in the Leipzig win. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “I stole the goal from Mbappe, but that’s because I knew he’d score another one. So, no problem.” The young Turk also pointed to the influence of playing at the Santiago Bernabeu, where the home crowd provides an additional motivation for the team. “It’s a key factor because when we play at home, in front of our fans, we try to give it our all for them.” Attention now turns to Sunday’s El Clasico , with Guler recognising the importance of the meeting and promising that Madrid will be ready to compete for the victory. “It’s a big match, a top-class fixture, and we’ll give it our all to win. We’re ready,” he concluded.

item.title: Mbappe and Arda Guler send strong message to Barcelona ahead of El Clasico: ‘We’ll give everything’
item.description: Mbappe and Arda Guler send strong message to Barcelona ahead of El Clasico: ‘We’ll give everything’ Real Madrid stars Kylian Mbappe and Arda Guler have turned their attention to Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona. After securing a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Champions League, both players have stressed the importance of the encounter as Jose Mourinho’s side look to reduce the six-point gap in La Liga . Speaking after Madrid’s Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig, Mbappe explained how the squad had deliberately avoided distractions before the European encounter. Mbappe explains Real Madrid’s approach to El Clasico As quoted by FCB World , Mbappe acknowledged that facing Barça carries a different significance from other fixtures. “El Clasico is completely different,” the French forward said. “We were only thinking about the Leipzig match. As for what will happen on Sunday, we can think about it now.” Mbappe is confident of his team putting on a show against Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Mbappe insisted that the squad had not allowed the upcoming Clasico to influence its preparations for Leipzig. “Before that, the team wasn’t thinking about Sunday’s match.” It is the kind of mentality Mourinho always insists on: players should focus on what lies immediately ahead of them. As a manager, he may be forced to consider the Barcelona fixture when making changes to the line-up, but the players cannot afford to get distracted. Arda Guler confident Madrid can challenge Barcelona Guler was equally clear about Madrid’s intentions when asked about the Barcelona encounter. “It’s a big match, a match of the highest level, and we’ll give everything we have to win,” the Turkey midfielder declared. He also emphasised the expectations that come with representing Real Madrid. “We are Real Madrid, and we have to win every match. We’re ready.” For Barcelona, it is a clear message that Los Blancos are completely focussed on the Barça clash and want to give it their best possible effort. Arda Guler has sent a strong message to Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Madrid cannot afford to fall further behind in the title race, particularly with Flick’s side already enjoying a six-point advantage. The Catalan club need to ensure they do exactly that. Barça should put on a statement performance on Sunday to effectively send a message to the rest of La Liga . A victory would extend their lead to nine points and deliver a significant psychological boost after the disappointment against PSG . Sunday’s clash promises to be exciting for both Barça and Madrid fans, and it remains to be seen how the game turns out.

item.title: Bayern Munich interested in Kone for January
item.description: Bayern Munich interested in Kone for January Manu Koné is one of the most important players in Gasperini’s Roma. Born in 2001, he is a pillar of the midfield: alongside Cristante, he forms a well-matched duo that combines balance and dynamism. In the final hours of the summer transfer window, Chelsea attempted to convince the Giallorossi to sell the former Borussia Mönchengladbach player, but the Roman club immediately closed the deal. Koné remains one of the Roma players attracting the most interest from the European big clubs. Koné has attracted the attention of Bayern Munich. According to Calciomercato.it, the Bavarian club is particularly interested in the 2001-born player, so much so that they’re attempting to land him as early as the next winter transfer window. For Gian Piero Gasperini and Roma, the player is unsellable, a crucial asset to maintain the balance of a team that is performing exceptionally well. The only way to change this scenario is with a monstrous offer from Bayern Munich.

item.title: Another Man Utd meltdown! Matheus Cunha & Michael Carrick caught in FURIOUS off-camera row as Champions League disaster sparks dressing room revolt
item.description: Manchester United’s season has plunged into further chaos following a humiliating Champions League defeat that saw internal tensions boil over. Reports have emerged of a heated confrontation between head coach Michael Carrick and forward Matheus Cunha as the Red Devils' winless run continues to haunt Old Trafford. Tensions boil over in Italy The crisis enveloping Manchester United deepened significantly on Wednesday night following a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como. Cesc Fabregas' side dismantled their English visitors in the Champions League, extending United's dismal winless streak to seven matches. Nico Paz orchestrated the rout with a memorable brace, scoring his first inside two minutes to instantly deflate the travelling support. While the result itself was disastrous, touchline developments have sparked even greater concern. According to The Sun' s Samuel Luckhurst , Carrick was involved in a 'relatively robust' altercation with Cunha that television cameras missed. Fans also picked up on the palpable friction between the Brazilian forward and his manager during a chaotic first-half display in Italy. Half-time changes highlight rift The tension between Cunha and Carrick culminated in immediate tactical changes at the interval. The head coach ruthlessly withdrew the Brazilian forward at half-time, introducing Amad Diallo in a desperate bid to inject life into his struggling side. Carlos Baleba was also brought on as United attempted to salvage any pride from the wreckage. These sweeping alterations ultimately proved ineffective. Just four minutes into the second period, Anastasios Douvikas capitalised on further defensive fragility to trigger a relentless wave of attacks from the hosts. Paz soon added his second following a glaring United error, punishing a visiting side that looked completely disjointed and bereft of ideas. The off-camera clash serves as a stark indicator of the rapidly deteriorating atmosphere behind the scenes. With United outplayed in every department, the frustrated exchanges on the touchline highlight a squad fracturing under immense pressure just two months into the campaign. FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Fernandes questions tactical approach The Cunha altercation is merely the latest sign of a broader dressing room revolt. Just a week after Lisandro Martinez publicly slammed the club's hierarchy over a lack of squad reinforcements following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, Bruno Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s game plan . Reports have emerged of a heated confrontation between head coach Michael Carrick and forward Matheus Cunha as the Red Devils' winless run continues to haunt Old Trafford. Tensions boil over in Italy The crisis enveloping Manchester United deepened significantly on Wednesday night following a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como. Cesc Fabregas' side dismantled their English visitors in the Champions League, extending United's dismal winless streak to seven matches. Nico Paz orchestrated the rout with a memorable brace, scoring his first inside two minutes to instantly deflate the travelling support. While the result itself was disastrous, touchline developments have sparked even greater concern. According to The Sun' s Samuel Luckhurst , Carrick was involved in a 'relatively robust' altercation with Cunha that television cameras missed. Fans also picked up on the palpable friction between the Brazilian forward and his manager during a chaotic first-half display in Italy. Half-time changes highlight rift The tension between Cunha and Carrick culminated in immediate tactical changes at the interval. The head coach ruthlessly withdrew the Brazilian forward at half-time, introducing Amad Diallo in a desperate bid to inject life into his struggling side. Carlos Baleba was also brought on as United attempted to salvage any pride from the wreckage. These sweeping alterations ultimately proved ineffective. Just four minutes into the second period, Anastasios Douvikas capitalised on further defensive fragility to trigger a relentless wave of attacks from the hosts. Paz soon added his second following a glaring United error, punishing a visiting side that looked completely disjointed and bereft of ideas. The off-camera clash serves as a stark indicator of the rapidly deteriorating atmosphere behind the scenes. With United outplayed in every department, the frustrated exchanges on the touchline highlight a squad fracturing under immense pressure just two months into the campaign. FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Fernandes questions tactical approach The Cunha altercation is merely the latest sign of a broader dressing room revolt. Just a week after Lisandro Martinez publicly slammed the club's hierarchy over a lack of squad reinforcements following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, Bruno Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s game plan . The Portuguese midfielder expressed clear frustration over the coaching staff's decision to avoid a man-to-man press, claiming it allowed Como to build early confidence. "It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early," the United captain told reporters. "Conceding early makes us go into [the] game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation." Carrick swiftly fired back, aiming pointed criticism at his players' work ethic rather than the tactical setup. The 45-year-old labelled the squad's application as unacceptable, bluntly stating: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win." Carrick fighting to save his job FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Manchester United now find themselves navigating a full-blown crisis both on and off the pitch. With seven consecutive matches without a victory, Carrick faces immense pressure to bridge the growing divide within his squad and restore basic defensive discipline. The glaring lack of on-field effort, compounded by public player dissent, leaves the Old Trafford hierarchy with critical decisions to make. The Red Devils must urgently find a way to halt this alarming slide, or they risk their entire season unravelling before the busy winter schedule even begins.

item.title: Continuing To Improve The Cleveland Browns Heading Towards 2027 - Offensive Review
item.description: theOBR While I regularly write about next season and roster predictions, this looks more at what the team is likely to do. In this piece I want to focus on where the Browns need to improve to get to above average in each position room for 2027. It will focus much more on the starters rather than seeing anything in terms of depth. They have a fantastic amount of cash and draft picks at their disposal to keep adding more to this young talented roster. Quarterback The arguments can continue of if Deshaun Watson is good enough to be a bridge quarterback in 2027 or not, when it comes to winning consistently, it doesn't really matter. Bridge quarterbacks and players you find in free agency, aren't going to take you to the Super Bowl in a loaded AFC. I don't see them going the route of trading multiple picks for a player after how it went previously. So that means the plan will be to take a quarterback next season in the draft. April is far too far away to worry about where the Browns will pick and who the best quarterbacks will be. The season is more about working out if Watson can be the bridge than anything else. Running Back At running back it feels like they need a second back to pair with Judkins in a 1A and 1B scenario like when they had Chubb and Hunt previously. They have plenty of change of pace backs to chose from between Sampson, Sanders and potentially McLaughlin. Luckily it is possible to pick up the type of backs they need in free agency at a relatively decent price. Wide Receiver After years of struggling to get quality at the position, they have three starting quality receivers. They will either need to keep Jeudy next season or add another via free agency, trade or the draft. I would keep Jeudy and then focus on adding more in the draft on day three with the hope you can develop someone. Tight End They need to find more at tight end. While Fannin has plenty of promise he has the potential to be Kyle Pitts type player who can be a massive part of the passing offense but low value in the run game. While they could focus on chasing a run blocking tight end, it will be limiting to have a clear run blocker and a clear pass catcher. This gives a tell to the opposition each time one is on the field. They would be better suited looking to add a more all-around tight end. Even if this effectively moves Fannin to being a hybrid tight end/wide receiver alongside a new tight end, Boston and Concepcion. Offensive Line Everything has been looking very positive on the offensive line over the last few weeks. While people questioned Howard, he has really turned it around and is looking like the $21m a year tackle they traded for. There is a very real chance they run it back in 2027 when it comes to their starters. With four of the starters likely locked in, it is just a question of does Elgton Jenkins return in 2027 or not. Even if this effectively moves Fannin to being a hybrid tight end/wide receiver alongside a new tight end, Boston and Concepcion. Offensive Line Everything has been looking very positive on the offensive line over the last few weeks. While people questioned Howard, he has really turned it around and is looking like the $21m a year tackle they traded for. There is a very real chance they run it back in 2027 when it comes to their starters. With four of the starters likely locked in, it is just a question of does Elgton Jenkins return in 2027 or not. As things stand it would be likely but there is a long season to go and he will turn 31 towards the end of the calendar year. Coaching When it comes to the offensive coaching staff, they need to focus on fixing the run game. It was semi working during the Ravens game, but this feels more like a one off than fixing it at this stage. It will be interesting to see if they can do anything over the next few weeks, but after the bye week could be the most telling spell. Conclusion Considering the starting shopping list for the offensive side of the ball currently sits at drafting a quarterback, a free agency running back and adding a tight end that can block, it isn't too extreme. Hitting on the quarterback will always be incredibly hard as teams have proven they haven't found a decent way to judge which college quarterbacks will and won't be successful. If they can fix this run game it could be a top offense in the league if they can make the right selection. It is why coming into this season I was incredibly high on the Browns in 2027 and I see no reason to pause the optimism.

item.title: ‘Wasn’t a top pick’-Super Bowl champion explains why Shedeur Sanders has struggled at Browns
item.description: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images Three-time Super Bowl champion Willie McGinest has explained why Shedeur Sanders has struggled to establish himself as the Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback, arguing that the young signal-caller did not arrive in the NFL with the same pressure as a top draft pick. Sanders has spent much of the current season watching from the sidelines as Deshaun Watson leads Cleveland under head coach Todd Monken. The Browns have made a strong start with Watson at the helm, leaving Sanders facing questions about his future and growing speculation over a potential trade. Willie McGinest says Shedeur Sanders must prove himself on the field McGinest believes Sanders’ draft position played a role in the expectations placed on him when he entered the league. Speaking about the Browns quarterback, the former New England Patriots linebacker said: “Shedeur didn’t put the pressure on the position by coming into the league. I mean that by saying he wasn’t like a top pick. Now, if you’re a number one pick, if you’re a top 10 pick, then you put the pressure on the position right away.” McGinest pointed to Russell Wilson as an example of a later-round pick who quickly forced his way into the starting conversation with the Seattle Seahawks. He argued that Sanders had not yet produced the same evidence to convince Cleveland that he deserved the job. “I know there’s a lot of hype and it’s the hype behind the name or the lineage where you come from or what you are actually doing on the football field. At some point, if he’s doing what he needs to do on the football field, he’ll get an opportunity,” McGinest added. Sanders did start eight games for Cleveland last season after Dillon Gabriel suffered a concussion, throwing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. His tendency to hold the ball for too long was also a concern, with his average time to throw reaching 3.24 seconds from his debut in Week 11, the highest figure in the NFL over that period. Watson has since strengthened his position as Cleveland’s starter, helping the Browns build a 4-2 record across their first six games. Sanders has also signed with Young Money APAA Sports for representation, a move that has fuelled speculation about his future. However, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones suggested a trade before the deadline would still be a surprise. Sanders now needs to make the most of his opportunities if he is to change the Browns’ thinking about his role. item.title: New Mexico State leans on James Jones, defense to outlast Sam Houston, 30-24
item.description: New Mexico State celebrates after 30-24 win over Sam Houston on October 22, 2026 | Steve Helwick Sam Houston had a chance to defend its home turf in a standalone Wednesday night Weekday CUSA matchup. Instead, New Mexico State left Huntsville with a long-awaited breakthrough. Behind a career-best performance from running back James Jones and a suffocating defensive effort, the Aggies defeated the Bearkats 30-24 at Bowers Stadium, securing their first road victory of the 2026 season. “We did a good job coming out and getting the first victory of the season,” New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez said. “I thought our guys played a good game, played a good four-quarter game, and it was really good to see at the end, with four minutes left, them kicking the ball deep and us being able to just run the clock out. Proud of our guys and happy for them.” The star of the night was Jones, who continued to lead the CUSA in rushing. The New Mexico State running back recorded his fourth 100-yard game of 2026 and shattered his career-high with 178 yards. He also opened the Aggies’ scoring in the second quarter with his lone touchdown of the night. “It’s a blessing,” Jones said of his performance. “I thank the Lord for every opportunity that He gave me. I appreciate what He’s given me. And my o-line, I can’t do it without them. Them up front fighting, our defense getting stops, we’re all playing together. It isn’t even on me, it’s up front.” Jones saved his best work for the final minutes. Clinging to a 6-point lead, New Mexico State leaned on its star running back to drain the final 4:00 of clock and deny the Bearkats an opportunity at a comeback victory. Jones gained 39 yards on four carries during the final drive, converting a 4th-and-2 with 29 seconds remaining to seal the Aggies’ first one-score victory since November 2025. “The final four minutes, I told my coach — Coach (David) Yost does a great job calling plays — but I was telling him, ‘I need the ball in my hands. I’m gonna ice it,’” Jones said. “Then the o-line was doing their thing up front, and then I popped one. That’s what got us in that situation — the o-line up front.” Despite the victory, New Mexico State’s offense had to overcome a pair of costly mistakes early in the game. Roughly two minutes into the contest, the Aggies fell behind 7-0 when Sam Houston wide receiver Terrence Guillory II blocked a punt and Railyn Adams recovered the loose ball in the end zone. Then in the second quarter, New Mexico State’s incomplete lateral pass in its own territory was ruled a fumble, and the Bearkats cashed in with a field goal. New Mexico State’s defense ensured those miscues did not prove costly. The Aggies allowed just 13 yards in the first half, surrendering 20 in the opening quarter before holding Sam Houston to -7 yards in the second. Roughly two minutes into the contest, the Aggies fell behind 7-0 when Sam Houston wide receiver Terrence Guillory II blocked a punt and Railyn Adams recovered the loose ball in the end zone. Then in the second quarter, New Mexico State’s incomplete lateral pass in its own territory was ruled a fumble, and the Bearkats cashed in with a field goal. New Mexico State’s defense ensured those miscues did not prove costly. The Aggies allowed just 13 yards in the first half, surrendering 20 in the opening quarter before holding Sam Houston to -7 yards in the second. The Bearkats finished with just nine first downs and 11 rushing yards, repeatedly struggling to win at the line of scrimmage. “I thought our defense played lights out,” Sanchez said. “Other than that very first snap of the second half, the guys did a fantastic job of creating pressure on the quarterback all night. We got some important turnovers and they did a really good job.” Sanchez also credited his offense for its response, and New Mexico State captured its first lead in the final seconds of the first half on a 2-play, 43-yard touchdown drive that consumed just 18 seconds. “Offensively, it was really good to see us put that touchdown on the board before halftime and come out early in the second half and get another touchdown,” Sanchez said. The Aggies’ defense came up with two crucial turnovers, each setting up a short field that led to a touchdown. In the second quarter, Josiah Charles intercepted Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke and returned the ball to the 1-yard line, setting up Jones’ touchdown. Late in the third quarter, Kaian Roberts-Day blew up a flea-flicker in the backfield and recovered the fumble, setting up TJ Washington Jr. for a rushing touchdown. “We’ve lost the turnover battle three weeks in a row,” said Sanchez, whose team was a minus-5 in turnover margin prior to Wednesday. “It’s really gotten in the way. You go all the way back to the Hawaii game, obviously the UNM game, the FIU game, and we weren’t winning the turnover battle. We had one really bad turnover at the end, but to win the turnover battle tonight made a big difference in the game.” Sam Houston’s offense finally found the explosive play it desperately needed to open the second half. After leaving the game in the second quarter with a leg injury, Locke returned to action and connected with Tim Burns Jr. for an 81-yard touchdown on the first snap after halftime, handing the Bearkats a 17-14 lead. Locke’s longest pass since Week 2 ended the team’s 12-quarter drought without an offensive touchdown, dating back to Sept. 26. Locke was briefly replaced by true freshman backup Brett Holloway before finishing the game with 235 passing yards. Sam Houston head coach Phil Longo explained the injury situation postgame. “They thought it was a fibula fracture, and they X-ray’d him, and you’re looking at losing your starting quarterback for the year,” Longo said. “Then 20 minutes goes by and no fracture, and they tape him up, we’re gonna treat him, and he comes back out and he couldn’t really move laterally, so we held him out for a little bit. We ran him around the sideline to see if he could move enough to do the things he needs to do. When he proved to me that he could do that and the trainers gave me the okay, we put him back on the field. For playing hurt, he actually played fairly decent in the second half.” The Bearkats’ momentum after Locke’s touchdown pass was brief. New Mexico State responded three minutes later with a touchdown strike from Adam Damante to AJ Williams III. The touchdown sparked a 16-0 run that put the Aggies back in control. It wasn’t Williams’ only highlight Wednesday night. The 6’4” wide receiver had an additional contested catch in the end zone, finishing the night with two touchdowns — both which handed New Mexico State the lead. “AJ has been waiting on this,” Jones said. “I’m very happy for him that everybody got to see what he can do, because he’s been doing it in practice all year.” Sam Houston eventually responded cutting the deficit to 30-24 with an MJ Dowdy rushing touchdown with four minutes remaining. But the Bearkats could not regain possession, as Jones and the Aggies’ offensive line dominated the final series. “I thought we challenged them from a heart and emotional and a grind standpoint in the second half, and they responded,” Longo said. “But too little, too late, obviously, so that’s kinda how the game went. We responded, played more physical, played with some more emotion and some passion offensively in the second half but came up short because it wasn’t enough.” Longo also commented on Sam Houston’s recurring offensive struggles in a night they were outgained by the visitor 203-11 on the ground. “I didn’t see yardage, that’s for sure,” Longo said on the offensive performance. “We addressed a lot of the issues we’d had the past two weeks. I think a lot of people understand we’re struggling up front because of some injuries. You gotta plug in the next guy and you gotta go. We even tried to redirect our plan this week, just to try and play maybe to the strengths of some of the guys we have in. But we just lack continuity up front right now, and it’s affecting us offensively.” Sam Houston (1-6, 0-3 CUSA) remains winless against FBS competition this season and has fallen to 3-16 in the Longo era. The Bearkats are on the brink of missing bowl eligibility for the second consecutive season, and to preserve those hopes, they must respond on the road Tuesday at Missouri State. “There’s a sense of urgency from the get-go,” Longo said. “I want for us to manage some of the issues we’re having on offense and fix them. item.title: The Wayward Train: My Dad’s Notre Dame Thanksgiving Adventure in 1963
item.description: An unforgettable Thanksgiving, a football game at Yankee Stadium, and a train ride that took an unexpected detour through Canada. Since Notre Dame has a bye week, I thought we’d take this week’s Throwback Thursday a little off the rails. Literally. Instead of revisiting a memorable victory or one of those classic Notre Dame football games that still makes us smile, I’m sharing a story from my dad’s college days. It’s a story that involves Thanksgiving on Long Island, a football game at Yankee Stadium, one of the most difficult moments in American history, and a train ride home that turned into an international adventure. Oh, and there’s a photograph of my dad sleeping upside down in his train seat. Yes, you read that correctly. But before we get to the train, we need to go back to Thanksgiving 1963. A Thanksgiving Invitation My dad was a student at Notre Dame when his classmate Mike Fiore invited him and a few friends to spend Thanksgiving with his family on Long Island. The plan was to enjoy the holiday with Mike’s family, explore a little of New York, and attend Notre Dame’s Thanksgiving Day football game against Syracuse at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Mike was studying civil engineering at Notre Dame, following in the footsteps of his father, who was also a Notre Dame graduate. My dad remembers Mike’s father as a highly accomplished civil engineer who had worked on bridge projects. The Fiore family welcomed the young men into their home for the Thanksgiving holiday, treating them to a wonderful dinner and giving them the opportunity to explore Long Island and New York City during their visit. They arrived Wednesday evening, attended the Notre Dame–Syracuse game at Yankee Stadium on Thanksgiving morning, and spent the rest of the holiday weekend enjoying time with friends before heading back to South Bend on Sunday. For a group of college students, it sounded like a pretty terrific Thanksgiving getaway. But the timing made this particular holiday unlike any other. On November 22, 1963, just six days before Notre Dame and Syracuse would meet at Yankee Stadium, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. When I asked my dad what he remembered about that Thanksgiving, he told me the country was still very much in shock. It’s difficult to imagine what those days must have felt like for a group of young college students. They were away from campus, spending time with friends, and looking forward to a football game, but the entire nation was grieving. item.content:encoded: An unforgettable Thanksgiving, a football game at Yankee Stadium, and a train ride that took an unexpected detour through Canada. Since Notre Dame has a bye week, I thought we’d take this week’s Throwback Thursday a little off the rails. Literally. Instead of revisiting a memorable victory or one of those classic Notre Dame football games that still makes us smile, I’m sharing a story from my dad’s college days. It’s a story that involves Thanksgiving on Long Island, a football game at Yankee Stadium, one of the most difficult moments in American history, and a train ride home that turned into an international adventure. Oh, and there’s a photograph of my dad sleeping upside down in his train seat. Yes, you read that correctly. But before we get to the train, we need to go back to Thanksgiving 1963. A Thanksgiving Invitation My dad was a student at Notre Dame when his classmate Mike Fiore invited him and a few friends to spend Thanksgiving with his family on Long Island. The plan was to enjoy the holiday with Mike’s family, explore a little of New York, and attend Notre Dame’s Thanksgiving Day football game against Syracuse at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Mike was studying civil engineering at Notre Dame, following in the footsteps of his father, who was also a Notre Dame graduate. My dad remembers Mike’s father as a highly accomplished civil engineer who had worked on bridge projects. The Fiore family welcomed the young men into their home for the Thanksgiving holiday, treating them to a wonderful dinner and giving them the opportunity to explore Long Island and New York City during their visit. They arrived Wednesday evening, attended the Notre Dame–Syracuse game at Yankee Stadium on Thanksgiving morning, and spent the rest of the holiday weekend enjoying time with friends before heading back to South Bend on Sunday. For a group of college students, it sounded like a pretty terrific Thanksgiving getaway. But the timing made this particular holiday unlike any other. On November 22, 1963, just six days before Notre Dame and Syracuse would meet at Yankee Stadium, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. When I asked my dad what he remembered about that Thanksgiving, he told me the country was still very much in shock. It’s difficult to imagine what those days must have felt like for a group of young college students. They were away from campus, spending time with friends, and looking forward to a football game, but the entire nation was grieving. And Notre Dame’s football team had experienced that historic week in a particularly unusual way. A Football Season Overshadowed by History In 2018, Notre Dame published a fascinating retrospective titled “Yankee Stadium, Circa 1963,” written by Matt Storin, who had served as the senior manager of the 1963 Fighting Irish football team. Storin, a member of Notre Dame’s Class of 1964 who went on to a distinguished journalism career, offered a firsthand look at a difficult season and an unforgettable Thanksgiving week. Notre Dame had been scheduled to face Iowa on November 23, the day after Kennedy’s assassination. According to Storin, the Irish had already arrived in Iowa City and settled into their hotel when the game was canceled. The team returned to South Bend on Sunday morning, only to turn around and travel to New York on Wednesday for its Thanksgiving matchup with Syracuse. The Irish were struggling through a season in which victories had been hard to come by. Under interim head coach Hugh Devore, Notre Dame had won just two of its first eight games. There was also uncertainty beyond the football field. Storin recalled the economic anxiety surrounding South Bend as Studebaker announced plans to end automobile production in the city. Between the assassination, the struggling football program, and concerns about the local economy, it was a particularly difficult time for the Notre Dame community. Yet the football season continued. Storin remembered the team arriving in New York and checking into the Waldorf Astoria. The traveling squad numbered fewer than 40 players, and the players had little time to prepare once they reached the city. The Thanksgiving Day game would kick off at 10:30 in the morning, an unusual start time by today’s standards, before a crowd of 56,672 at the original Yankee Stadium. For Storin, walking through the third-base dugout and onto the famous playing field was an unforgettable experience. For my dad and his friends, it was another chance to cheer on the Irish. Unfortunately, the game itself would provide yet another frustrating chapter in Notre Dame’s 1963 season. Notre Dame vs. Syracuse: A Familiar Ending The 1963 Notre Dame Football Review described Yankee Stadium as an unusual setting for college football. The enormous grandstands towered above the players, casting long shadows across the field and blocking much of the late-November sunlight. The Irish had experienced several heartbreaking losses that season, and the Syracuse game would follow a painfully familiar pattern. Syracuse controlled much of the early action but repeatedly failed to capitalize on scoring opportunities. On one promising drive, Orange running back Jim Nance fumbled near the Notre Dame goal line, and Tom Longo recovered for the Irish. Eventually, Syracuse broke through when Wally Mahle connected with Billy Hunter on a six-yard touchdown pass. Dick Arrington blocked the extra-point attempt, leaving Notre Dame trailing 6-0. Late in the second quarter, the Irish finally found some offensive momentum. Starting at their own 14-yard line, Notre Dame put together an impressive 86-yard scoring drive. Nick Rassas gained 20 yards around right end, Jim Kelly hauled in a 15-yard pass from Sandy Bonvechio, and Tommy MacDonald helped move the Irish deep into Syracuse territory. Then Notre Dame reached into its bag of tricks. Bonvechio pitched the ball to halfback Frank Budka, who threw a touchdown pass to MacDonald in the end zone. Ken Ivan added the extra point, giving Notre Dame a 7-6 lead with just one minute remaining in the first half. For a team that had struggled so much throughout the season, perhaps this would finally be the afternoon when everything came together. The Irish defense certainly did its part. Bill Pfeiffer intercepted a Syracuse pass in the third quarter, and MacDonald added another interception to his impressive career total. Bob Lehmann and Ken Maglicic also helped thwart Syracuse scoring opportunities as the Irish clung to their narrow lead. But the fourth quarter brought another heartbreaking finish. With 3:28 remaining, Syracuse quarterback Rich King connected with Mike Koski for the go-ahead touchdown. A successful two-point conversion extended the Orange lead to 14-7. Notre Dame couldn’t answer, and the Irish fell to Syracuse by seven points. In his 2018 recollection, Storin described the loss as the fourth time that season Notre Dame had surrendered a game-deciding score late in the contest. He also remembered an exchange with a Syracuse player after the game. The player sympathized with Notre Dame’s difficult afternoon, and Storin replied that it had been much like the rest of the season. Sometimes, that’s just the way football goes. One interesting detail from Storin’s account is that Notre Dame wore green jerseys that Thanksgiving Day. The Irish wouldn’t wear green again until the famous 1977 game against USC. And although nobody knew it at the time, the 1963 season was about to become an important turning point in Notre Dame football history. Just 18 days after the Syracuse game, Notre Dame announced that Northwestern head coach Ara Parseghian would take over the program. The Irish would go from a 2-7 season in 1963 to a 9-1 record in 1964, narrowly missing a national championship. But back on Thanksgiving weekend in 1963, none of that was known.
