item.title: ‘Clears Caitlin Clark,’ ‘Finals MVP Loading’ — WNBA World Raves As Angel Reese, Dream Crush Valkyries To Take 2-1 Finals Lead
item.description: 'Clears Caitlin Clark,' 'Finals MVP Loading' -- WNBA World Raves As Angel Reese, Dream Crush Valkyries To Take 2-1 Finals Lead Angel Reese is making her presence felt on the biggest stage of her young WNBA career. After the Atlanta Dream’s 79-65 Game 2 road win tied the series, the Defensive Player of the Year helped her team take control of the WNBA Finals with another double-double outing against the Golden State Valkyries on Wednesday. Playing in front of a sold-out crowd at State Farm Arena, the Dream, led by the three-time All-Star, cruised to a 97-71 Game 3 win. Reese’s performance sparked a wave of reactions across the WNBA world, with fans hyping her impact and some already projecting her to take home Finals MVP. WNBA World Raves As Angel Reese Powers Dream to Game 3 Finals Win The Valkyries looked poised throughout much of their postseason run, but the Finals have presented a different challenge. Reese came into Game 3 locked in, determined to keep attacking after vowing to get more aggressive offensively following Atlanta’s Game 1 loss. She delivered, finishing with a game-high 21 points, 12 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals while shooting 7-for-12 from the field. She also knocked down both of her 3-point attempts. The WNBA’s X account hyped her all-around performance, posting : “Angel Reese is a GAME CHANGER.” “Oh, she CLEARS Caitlin Clark,” one Reese fan gushed . “FINALS MVP LOADING……Angel Shutting The Haters Up,” another supporter added , already looking ahead. The praise for the 24-year-old kept coming, with one fan writing , “She is balling.” One post took the Clark comparison a step further, asking , “Angel Reese FMVP before Caitlin Clark makes a conference final???” Reese’s latest outing followed a historic 30-point performance in Game 2. She has now recorded a double-double in each of her first three career Finals games. According to ESPN Insights , she is the first player in WNBA history to pull that off. She also joins A’ja Wilson as one of only two players to record back-to-back games with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in a single Finals. Reese’s confidence was on full display from the jump in Game 3. After converting an and-one against Aminata Gueye, the former Chicago Sky forward turned and talked a little trash toward the Valkyries’ bench, bringing extra energy to an already lit home crowd. MORE: ‘The Angel Reese Effect,’ ‘They Said Nobody Watches Unless Caitlin (Clark) Is Playing’ — WNBA World Buzzes As Finals Opener Sets Viewership Record That said, Atlanta’s Game 3 dominance extended well beyond its star. The Dream shot 49.3% from the field, compared with Golden State’s 34.8%, and outscored the Valkyries 44-20 in the paint. That edge showed just how hard Atlanta has attacked a defense that had been a major strength throughout Golden State’s postseason run. item.title: “A reserve team” – Carrick’s former Man Utd teammate believes he has lost the plot
item.description: “A reserve team” – Carrick’s former Man Utd teammate believes he has lost the plot Dimitar Berbatov suggests the writing is on the wall for Michael Carrick following Manchester United’s embarrassing defeat to Como. The Red Devils landed in Italy on the back of a six-match winless run. So while the team was desperate for a revitalising result, they ended up suffering their worst defeat under Carrick, as Cesc Fabregas’ men ran circles around them en route to a 4-1 victory. Nico Paz was the ultimate star of the show with a brace and an assist, while Joshua Zirkzee’s late consolation goal changed little in the narrative. Dimitar Berbatov blasts ‘terrible’ Man Utd (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) This defeat will pile more pressure on Carrick, who has been walking on increasingly thin ice for weeks. To make matters even worse for the under-fire coach, his tactics were publicly questioned by his captain Bruno Fernandes, who suggested that United played into Como’s favour by not pressing them, prompting a swift reply from the Englishman. Therefore, many believe the 45-year-old manager wouldn’t be able to survive the storm, and one of them happens to be a former teammate. After the game, Berbatov roasted Man Utd’s ‘terrible’ display by comparing them to a reserve team. The Bulgarian believes Carrick won’t be able to turn things around. “It was a terrible, terrible night and a terrible game for Manchester United,” said the retired striker during his appearance on TNT Sports (via Metro ). “Como outplayed them in every way possible. It was like they were playing a reserve team, almost. “Are these the players who can compete for a club like Manchester United? Is it the right manager? Those questions will be asked after this kind of performance,” added Berbatov” “It’s going to be harder and harder for Michael Carrick to turn it around. It was like watching men against kids.” Will Michael Carrick survive the storm? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) As Berbatov points out, Carrick has seemingly lost the plot. He may have already reached the point of no return. Perhaps he won’t even be given the chance to rebound after such a miserable performance, as a Thursday-morning sacking cannot be ruled out. And yet, Carrick might be the least of United’s problems. After all, the toxic atmosphere at the club has long preceded the 45-year-old’s reign. Lisandro Martinez perhaps made an ill-advised decision by calling out the hierarchy , but his words carried important facts, as Man Utd’s issues start at the very top of the pyramid. item.title: NDSU Has 2 Intriguing Projected Bowl Matchups
item.description: NDSU is projected to make the Hawaii Bowl. Getty North Dakota State is set for bowl eligibility, and speculation on bowl game matchups are in full swing. ESPN has two interesting projected bowl matchups for the Bison after Week 7 of the college football season. Analyst Mark Schlabach picked the Bison to face Fresno State in the Sheraton Hawaii Bowl, and fellow analyst Kyle Bonagura has the Bison facing San Diego State in the same bowl. Both analysts have Boise State nabbing the Group of Six spot in the College Football Playoff as the No. 12 seed. item.title: Beşiktaş vs Crystal Palace: Preview, Team News And Expected Lineups
item.description: Crystal Palace have travelled to Istanbul to face Beşiktaş in their third game of the Europa League league phase. Palace will be looking to record not only a positive result, but a much improved performance following the disappointment across the last seven days. Palace fell to defeat in Lyon after another poor first half performance, followed by what can only be described as a demolition job against rivals Brighton. Now, Palace face potentially their biggest test to date, travelling to the football hotbed that is Istanbul to play in one of Europe’s most hostile atmospheres. Team news and fitness update In his pre-match press conference ahead of the game, Sage revealed the latest injury news in preparation for the game, which included a slightly surprising name. Ben Chilwell is back with the squad and travelled to Turkey, but that good news was paired with the update that Takehiro Tomiyasu will not be available until after the next international break, which takes place between the 9th and 17th of November. Dean Henderson started to train with the team again on Monday but has not travelled, his fitness being assessed ahead of a potential return to the side at the weekend. Quinten Timber will also miss the game, but Sage did not elaborate on that news. This will be the most notable absence for Palace of them all, as Timber has started almost every single game since he signed for the club. Tyrick Mitchell Sets Clear Ambition For The Season - Community Post In an interview with the club, Tyrick Mitchell has made clear his ambitions going into the remainder of the season. The Palace left-back is keen to recreate the success that he has lived with the club. Beşiktaş could be Palace’s toughest test In terms of the Eagle’s Europa League fixtures, an away trip to Beşiktaş should have been circled as one of the more difficult games that Palace would have to play in the league phase of the competition. Beşiktaş JK are one of the most decorated Turkish sides in football history. They’ve won 16 Turkish League titles, eleven Turkish Cups and ten Turkish Super Cups, but have never won a European trophy. Nicknamed ‘The Black Eagles’, Beşiktaş have enjoyed a flying start to their Europa League campaign. Managed by Vincenzo Italiano, they are currently 4th in the league phase having won both of their opening games. A 4-1 win at home to Marseille was followed by a 2-3 win away to Hoffenheim. Domestically, they’re struggling somewhat for form, currently sitting 4th in the Trendyol Süper Lig, winning five and losing three of their opening eight games. Their most recent outing was a 2-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, Mohammed Salah scoring the second last weekend. In terms of standout players that Palace fans need to look out for, Beşiktaş have a number of big names that are coming to the end of their careers. item.title: Former Fulham star Bryan Ruiz named Costa Rica head coach on permanent basis with mission to reach 2030 World Cup
item.description: FBL-CONCACAF-NATIONS-CRC-HAI - AFP The Costa Rican Football Federation (FCRF) has officially appointed legendary former captain Bryan Ruiz as the permanent manager of the men's national team following an impressive interim spell in the dugout. The 41-year-old ex-Fulham playmaker has been tasked with guiding his country back to the World Cup finals in 2030. Interim success secures permanent role The Costa Rican Football Federation Executive Committee finalised contract terms to hand their former skipper the permanent reins with a mandate to qualify for the 2030 global showpiece. Originally appointed on September 28 after Argentine boss Fernando Batista was dismissed, the 41-year-old immediately recalled veteran goalkeeper Keylor Navas. Back-to-back victories over Nicaragua (3-0) and Haiti (2-0) at Estadio Ricardo Saprissa subsequently preserved the nation's CONCACAF Nations League A status. View this post on Instagram Inexperienced tactician assembles trusted backroom The appointment marks Ruiz's first permanent senior managerial role, having previously worked in the youth setup and as an assistant at Liga Deportiva Alajuelense, where he only oversaw two first-team games on an emergency basis. According to the federation's official statement , the decision provides continuity and consolidates a new stage by allowing their former talisman to bring his leadership and knowledge of the domestic and international game to the touchline. To support him, Ruiz has named former World Cup team-mates Wilmer Lopez and Christian Bolanos as assistant coaches alongside video analyst Ariel Gonzalez, while Wardy Alfaro will also join the coaching staff as an assistant in January. Iconic captain inherits rebuilding project During his playing days, the left-footed attacking midfielder represented Twente, PSV Eindhoven, Fulham, Sporting CP and Santos before retiring at Alajuelense in 2022. He also captained La Sele across three consecutive World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, famously spearheading their historic run to the 2014 quarter-finals in Brazil. However, he now takes over a side that has slipped down the FIFA rankings after missing out on the 2026 tournament under Mexican manager Miguel Herrera and enduring a string of Nations League setbacks under Batista. South American heavyweights test credentials Ruiz will take charge of his first matches as permanent boss during next month's international window when Costa Rica travel to face Ecuador on November 13 and Argentina four days later . Those demanding away friendlies will test whether a tactician with just four games of senior management can build on his early momentum. Strong performances in South America will be vital as he begins shaping a competitive squad.

item.title: Wales milestone for Callender as Metcalfe sisters start
item.description: Wales flanker Alex Callender joined Harlequins in 2024 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Flanker Alex Callender will win her 50th cap for Wales in Saturday's WXV Global Series game against Japan - while sisters Nel and Branwen Metcalfe will start their first Test together. Head coach Sean Lynn has made three personnel changes to the starting line-up from September's narrow defeat by USA at Cardiff Arms Park. Nel Metcalfe returns from injury on the wing, Seren Lockwood is back at scrum-half and Jorja Aiono gets the nod at lock. There are two positional changes with Carys Cox switching to centre and Keira Bevan starting at fly-half. Callender, co-captain with fellow back-row forward Amy Williams, will lead Wales out in Tokyo (10:30 BST) when bringing up her half-century of caps. Callender won her first cap in 2019 and hits 50 after returning impressively from injuries suffered before, during and after the 2025 World Cup. The 26-year-old made a comeback in June's uncapped fixture against the Barbarians, was named as player of the match against South Africa and scored against USA. "Whenever you talk about a Welsh person everything is about calon and passion - that's her in abundance," said Lynn. "Whenever she puts that jersey on she wears it with pride and wants to represent the nation. She galvanises this group incredibly, on the pitch and off it." Callender is a combative flanker but Lynn is quick to point out her deft touches. "Everybody has always seen Alex as a very passionate individual with phenomenal tackling and breakdown work," said the head coach. "But she has grown her game and is a really good operator in the line-out and the attack. "We've been trying to play her as a forward on the edges and she is excelling after working hard on her handling ability over pre-season. "We're looking to play an expansive game and having a back-row forward who is just like another back brings another dimension." Quiz: Name the 12 players given Wales debuts by Lynn Wales use fight for Lions spots as extra incentive Bevan back at 10 Bevan returns to pulling the strings from fly-half after an encouraging performance alongside Lockwood was ended when the scrum-half suffered a head injury against South Africa. The score was already 26-5 when the 19-year-old went off, which prompted the introduction of outside half Lleucu George. "They were super exciting in the first 30 minutes in South Africa game," said Lynn. "Keira just wants the ball in her hands, she wants to move the ball and her maturity with the kicking game is developing. "Her performance against USA as a scrum-half was very good as well but we saw the damage that Seren can do against South Africa, and also in the Barbarians fixture when she stood out." The 26-year-old made a comeback in June's uncapped fixture against the Barbarians, was named as player of the match against South Africa and scored against USA. "Whenever you talk about a Welsh person everything is about calon and passion - that's her in abundance," said Lynn. "Whenever she puts that jersey on she wears it with pride and wants to represent the nation. She galvanises this group incredibly, on the pitch and off it." Callender is a combative flanker but Lynn is quick to point out her deft touches. "Everybody has always seen Alex as a very passionate individual with phenomenal tackling and breakdown work," said the head coach. "But she has grown her game and is a really good operator in the line-out and the attack. "We've been trying to play her as a forward on the edges and she is excelling after working hard on her handling ability over pre-season. "We're looking to play an expansive game and having a back-row forward who is just like another back brings another dimension." Quiz: Name the 12 players given Wales debuts by Lynn Wales use fight for Lions spots as extra incentive Bevan back at 10 Bevan returns to pulling the strings from fly-half after an encouraging performance alongside Lockwood was ended when the scrum-half suffered a head injury against South Africa. The score was already 26-5 when the 19-year-old went off, which prompted the introduction of outside half Lleucu George. "They were super exciting in the first 30 minutes in South Africa game," said Lynn. "Keira just wants the ball in her hands, she wants to move the ball and her maturity with the kicking game is developing. "Her performance against USA as a scrum-half was very good as well but we saw the damage that Seren can do against South Africa, and also in the Barbarians fixture when she stood out." Nel makes it a Metcalfe double Nel and Branwen Metcalfe played at the 2025 Rugby World Cup [Huw Evans Picture Agency] The Metcalfe sisters played for Wales together for the first time when lock Branwen came off the bench for her first cap against Canada at the 2025 World Cup. They started the uncapped fixture against the Baa-Baas but join forces in the XV for the first time at Test level against Japan. Branwen, 20, starts her sixth successive Test and has a new second-row partner in fellow bright prospect Aiono. Nel, 21, returns on the wing rather than full-back for her first cap since the World Cup after a knee injury that forced her to sit out the Six Nations. "She was a shining light at the World Cup, which was tough for us," said Lynn. "Every time that she gets the ball, something will happen. She has got fitter, stronger and faster, and she's excited to go out there on Saturday." Wales are 11th in World Rugby's rankings, a spot above Japan. Last month the Sakura Fifteen lost 55-21 to Italy and were beaten twice by Ireland, 31-24 in the WXV Global Series and 43-19 in an extra Test. "Japan ran Ireland close in the first Test and they are very efficient in what they do, very regimented," said Lynn, who opts for six forwards on his bench. "They've got a very good maul and we are not going to be taking them lightly at all." How sport helps Bluck's autism journey Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls How Wales line up vs Japan Neumann; N Metcalfe, Cox, Bell, A Williams; Bevan, Lockwood; M Davies, K Jones, Tuipulotu, B Metcalfe, Aiono, K Williams (co-capt), Callender (co-capt), King. Replacements: Reardon, Pyrs, E Jones, Crabb, G Evans, B Lewis, George, Keight.

item.title: A new very hot favourite in the Premier League sack race
item.description: Matthias Jaissle looking focused on the touchline during a football match Last (2025-26) season the Premier League sack race didn’t last long. The runners had barely set off before a winner broke the finishing tape. Nuno was the winner last season of the 2025-26 Premier League sack race, Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis giving his manager the boot on 9 September 2025. When the remaining runners set off again, it was only 18 days later when on 27 September 2025 we saw Graham Potter sacked by West Ham. Incredibly, Marinakis then sacked Ange Postecoglou on 18 October 2025, only 39 days after he had replaced Nuno. In total, 11 Premier League managers were sacked last season, but we are still waiting for the first one of the 2026-27 season. So how things are looking for the 2026-27 running of this Premier League sack race now. Having sacked three managers in total during last season, the Nottingham Forest owner isn’t favourite to get there first this time. Oliver Glasner (Forest) finds himself joint fourth favourite alongside Matthias Jaissle (Newcastle United, pictured at the top) and Regis Le Bris (Sunderland) with those laying the odds. Third favourite is Alvaro Arbeloa (Fulham) and second fav is Pierre Sage (Palace). However, the very hot new clear odds on favourite is Michael Carrick at Manchester United . Man U have won none of their last seven matches (all competitions) and the latest was a 4-1 hammering by Como in the Champions League. The defeat could and should have been even heavier and the Man U goal came in added time when 4-0 down. Manchester United have only won two of 11 matches this season and they were against Sabah from Azerbaijan and Ipswich, the latter leading at Old Trafford before Man U got an incredible run of luck to turn that game around. To make matters worse for Michael Carrick, the disgraceful Bruno Fernandes (how on earth he was ever made Man U captain, a good effective player when he tries but as a leader…) then stabbed his manager in the back after the Como humiliation. Bruno Fernandes when asked what had gone wrong: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence.” Bruno Fernandes then asked specifically whether Michael Carrick had got his tactics wrong: “That’s on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” This is your captain speaking… In total, eleven Premier League managers were sacked during last (2025-26) season (with their replacements in brackets): 9 September 2025 – Nuno leaves Forest (Ange Postecoglou) 27 September 2025 – Graham Potter leaves West Ham (Nuno) 18 October 2025 – Ange Postecoglou leaves Forest (Sean Dyche) 2 November 2025 – Vitor Pereira leaves Wolves (Rob Edwards) 1 January 2026 – Enzo Maresca leaves Chelsea (Liam Rosenior) 5 January 2026 –

item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: Jürgen Klopp picks Barcelona over Real Madrid ahead of El Clásico
item.description: Jürgen Klopp picks Barcelona over Real Madrid ahead of El Clásico Jürgen Klopp will be watching El Clásico when Barcelona face Real Madrid at the weekend, and the Germany coach believes the Catalan side currently have the edge over their historic rivals. Speaking at half-time of Bayern Munich’s Champions League match against Arsenal, Klopp revealed that the clash between Spanish football’s two giants has been a constant throughout his life. “Of course I’ll watch El Clásico between Barcelona and Real Madrid. I’ve watched this game at every stage of my life,” Klopp said. His allegiance, however, has not always been based on which team he considers the strongest. Klopp explained that he used to favour Barcelona because he disliked the aggressive defensive approach associated with Real Madrid players such as Pepe. “In the past, I was more of a Barcelona supporter because I was against the actions of Pepe and other Madrid defenders,” he explained. These days, Klopp takes a more straightforward approach when deciding which side he wants to see win. “Today, I support the better team. And looking at things at the moment, that is probably Barcelona.” The comments offer a glimpse into Klopp’s long-standing interest in one of football’s biggest rivalries. He will also be interested in watching Karim Adeyemi for Barcelona, who has definitely improved his form over the past few weeks.

item.title: Mbappe, Courtois react after Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig: ‘We need to close the gap on Barcelona’
item.description: Mbappe, Courtois react after Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig: ‘We need to close the gap on Barcelona’ Kylian Mbappe has offered Vinicius Jr. a message of reassurance after the Brazilian endured a frustrating evening in Real Madrid’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Leipzig. The Frenchman has insisted that his disappointment reflects his determination to perform better for the team and its supporters. Vinicius was substituted in the 70th minute and walked towards the bench with his head down, but Mbappe stressed that the forward should remain confident in his ability. Meanwhile, Thibaut Courtois highlighted the importance of his first-half saves and explained why Madrid must carry their defensive improvement into Sunday’s crucial El Clasico against Barcelona. Mbappe explains why Vinicius should stay confident Vinicius did not produce his best performance against Leipzig and was replaced by Yan Diomande as Madrid managed the closing stages of the match. Rather than viewing his teammate’s visible frustration as a concern, Mbappe suggested it demonstrated how much the Brazilian wanted to contribute. “It’s fine. It’s fine that Vinícius is feeling down because he wants to give so much to the team and the fans. “He needs to stay calm and be proud of who he is. He’s a great player with immense quality,” Mbappe told Movistar Plus (h/t Mundo Deportivo ). The French forward also turned the focus towards his own standards, acknowledging that he expects more from himself despite Madrid’s convincing victory. Mbappe expressed his delight after win over RB Leipzig. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “I’m fine. I can do more. I’m one of those players who always have to push themselves further. It’s never enough for a player like me,” he explained. With three Champions League victories secured, Mbappe also emphasised the importance of collecting enough points to finish in the competition’s top eight. “We know that every point is important to make it into the top eight. We have to win as many matches as possible; we’ve won three.” Courtois reveals why his Leipzig saves mattered Real Madrid’s four-goal victory did not tell the whole story of the opening half. Courtois was called into action twice with the score still goalless, and his interventions helped prevent Leipzig from gaining an advantage before the Spanish side took control. “I feel great, I’m happy, and I’m working well. “Two important saves to keep a clean sheet at that stage and go into half-time ahead – that was important because the match can get away from you if you’re behind,” said the goalkeeper. The goalkeeper also explained how Real Madrid responded to the coaching staff’s half-time instructions, pointing to greater defensive intensity and the depth available across the squad. “Scoring first was important, and at half-time the manager told us to improve defensively. We improved, defended with more intensity – a good win. Courtois made some crucial saves against Leipzig. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty

We improved, defended with more intensity – a good win. Courtois made some crucial saves against Leipzig. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “The team is in great shape; we’re seeing that we can count on almost the entire squad. “There’s a lot of competition, and we’re all making each other better. “Now we have four away games, which is more difficult and we’re finding it tough, but we hope to go into the international break with four wins,” he said. Real Madrid shift their attention to Barcelona With the European fixture completed, Mbappe confirmed that the squad had deliberately avoided looking ahead to Barcelona before facing Leipzig. The Frenchman can now turn his attention to a Clasico that could have important consequences for Madrid’s position in the La Liga title race. “We’ve been focusing solely on today’s match. We can think about what happens on Sunday now. Before, the team wasn’t thinking about Sunday’s match.” Courtois was equally direct about the challenge awaiting Madrid, stressing that closing the gap on Barcelona requires a victory and a disciplined defensive performance. “We need to close the gap on them, and that can only be done by winning. We’re going into the match with confidence and hopefully we’ll defend well so we don’t concede.”

item.title: AC Milan’s last visit to the south coast they prepare for Bournemouth clash
item.description: AC Milan’s last visit to the south coast they prepare for Bournemouth clash AC Milan head to Bournemouth on Thursday in the Europa League, 18 years on from their last visit to the South Coast. Carlo Ancelotti’s side travelled to Portsmouth in November 2008 to face off against Pompey in a UEFA Cup clash. Portsmouth were massive underdogs with a team full of dependable but not flashy Premier League journeymen. David James, Younes Kaboul, Sylvain Distin, Papa Bouba Diop, Peter Crouch and Kanu all started. Even though they boasted a star-studded line-up that included Gennaro Gattuso, Kaká, Filippo Inzaghi and Andrey Shevchenko, Milan shockingly fell behind at Fratton Park. Managed by Tony Adams, Pompey kept the tie scoreless until half-time. Following the interval, they amazingly scored twice to stun the Rossoneri. Firstly, Kaboul got on the end of Glenn Johnson’s cross to head past Dida in front of a raucous Fratton End. Soon after, Kanu doubled the hosts’ advantage when he finished from close range. Ancelotti had just assembled his Avengers to rescue the tie when Kanu scored, sending Clarence Seedorf, Alexandre Pato and Ronaldinho on in between Portsmouth’s first and second strike. Ultimately, Milan were able to claw back a draw. Ronaldinho curled a free-kick past David James before Inzaghi broke Pompey hearts by poking home in stoppage time. Yet, the tie is still remembered as a famous night at Fratton Park with Ronaldinho labelling it as one of the ‘best atmospheres’ he played in. item.content:encoded: AC Milan’s last visit to the south coast they prepare for Bournemouth clash AC Milan head to Bournemouth on Thursday in the Europa League, 18 years on from their last visit to the South Coast. Carlo Ancelotti’s side travelled to Portsmouth in November 2008 to face off against Pompey in a UEFA Cup clash. Portsmouth were massive underdogs with a team full of dependable but not flashy Premier League journeymen. David James, Younes Kaboul, Sylvain Distin, Papa Bouba Diop, Peter Crouch and Kanu all started. Even though they boasted a star-studded line-up that included Gennaro Gattuso, Kaká, Filippo Inzaghi and Andrey Shevchenko, Milan shockingly fell behind at Fratton Park. Managed by Tony Adams, Pompey kept the tie scoreless until half-time. Following the interval, they amazingly scored twice to stun the Rossoneri. Firstly, Kaboul got on the end of Glenn Johnson’s cross to head past Dida in front of a raucous Fratton End. Soon after, Kanu doubled the hosts’ advantage when he finished from close range. Ancelotti had just assembled his Avengers to rescue the tie when Kanu scored, sending Clarence Seedorf, Alexandre Pato and Ronaldinho on in between Portsmouth’s first and second strike. Ultimately, Milan were able to claw back a draw. Ronaldinho curled a free-kick past David James before Inzaghi broke Pompey hearts by poking home in stoppage time. Yet, the tie is still remembered as a famous night at Fratton Park with Ronaldinho labelling it as one of the ‘best atmospheres’ he played in. Bournemouth will be hoping to go one better than their South Coast rivals on Thursday by getting the win, but Ruben Amorim’s team will prove a stern test after a fine start to the season.

item.title: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Valverde, Camavinga, Bernardo after Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig
item.description: Jose Mourinho talks Vinicius, Valverde, Camavinga, Bernardo after Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig Real Madrid maintained their post-international break winning run as they faced RB Leipzig in their latest UEFA Champions League game at the Santiago Bernabeu. After yet another underwhelming first half, the Merengues won this game 4-1, with goals from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Kylian Mbappe, and Yan Diomande. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed the press after this game and talked about several aspects of his team’s performance in this game. Vinicius Junior was once again significantly below his expected level in this match and his sadness was quite visible as he left the bench right after the full-time whistle. On the contrary, the Portuguese coach assured that he was actually happy for the Brazilian: “It’s something very personal. I think you can have your own perception, but I believe only he can tell you how he feels. As a coach, I’m happy with what he has done. People always expect more from Vini, for him to be decisive, but I liked his performance. He had more defensive responsibility than the other attackers, and he tracked back very well. It wasn’t a change because I wasn’t happy with him. It was because I have a strong bench and could bring on someone who could offer different things. You have to get used to me taking off a player who isn’t playing badly and replacing him with someone who can give me something different.” The Real Madrid coach asked the fans to put their support behind the winger: “Yes, he needs everyone’s support. He was booed away from home, and that can be motivating, but when it happens at your own ground, it hurts.” Mourinho was not too revealing when asked about Fede Valverde’s role in El Clasico: “I’m not talking about Sunday. You can ask me again on Saturday, but I won’t tell you whether he’ll play at right-back again. It wasn’t an easy match, and the 4-1 scoreline doesn’t reflect the first half. Fede played well.” The Portuguese coach went on to comment on several other lineup decisions: “He [Camavinga] had a great game. Obviously, against Sevilla, Arda and Tchouaméni did a good job in that area. I made too many changes, but I had confidence in the players because of what they show me. I really like Brahim every time he’s on the pitch. We’re back to the question of meritocracy. Perhaps Amazon could come up with something to measure that! Having Fede at right-back is frustrating for me because it means leaving two right-backs out.” The Real Madrid coach once again expressed his displeasure at referees for the next match being revealed too early: “This is completely out of context, but the appointment is officially announced 24 hours before the match. Fede played well.” The Portuguese coach went on to comment on several other lineup decisions: “He [Camavinga] had a great game. Having Fede at right-back is frustrating for me because it means leaving two right-backs out.” The Real Madrid coach once again expressed his displeasure at referees for the next match being revealed too early: “This is completely out of context, but the appointment is officially announced 24 hours before the match. I don’t like this kind of information coming out now. I’m not referring to them personally.” Despite the improved form, Mourinho was clear that the team is still not where he wants them to be: “Nothing is exactly where I want it to be, but we’re doing some things better now than before. Today, there was a goal I didn’t like, because it left the match open for us to win. The goal we conceded today came from a situation in which the opponent was comfortable, and I don’t like that.” The Portuguese coach was also full of praise for his compatriot, Bernardo Silva: “He’s a great player and had a great game. And we won the Premier League with Courtois in goal. Čech, the best of them all, played only in the cup competitions. “If I say this, Júlio César will call me in two minutes and say, ‘Oh, Courtois is the best, but you won the Champions League with me.’ He’ll call me in two minutes, I’m sure. I’ve always had this respect for my former players. But, you know… this guy is…” As Jose Mourinho mentioned, although the scoreline reflects otherwise, this was still quite a difficult game for Real Madrid. However, the Merengues have an even bigger challenge awaiting them, as they face an FC Barcelona side that has not lost in La Liga so far this season, and hopefully, Los Blancos will rise to the challenge in that game as well.

item.title: MVP MMA On Netflix One And Done?
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - MAY 16: Ronda Rousey forces Gina Carano into an armbar submission in their featherweight bout during the main card of Netflix's Ronda Rousey vs. Gina Carano at Intuit Dome on May 16, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images for Netflix) | Getty Images for Netflix Ronda Rousey vs. Gina Carano was the first live MMA event to ever feature on Netflix. It may also be the last for quite some time. Jake Paul and Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) intended to disrupt the MMA world with their collaboration with the streaming giant, but Netflix has fallen on hard times. Its stock price has dropped almost 30% in the last six months, prompting layoffs and overall corporate restructuring. Unfortunately, MVP MMA may end up on the cutting room floor as a result. Per combat sports insider Blake Avignon , Netflix is unlikely to host another MVP MMA event barring a main event like Francis Ngannou vs. Jon Jones , which is currently impossible due to “Bones” continued UFC contract. Without that level of a marquee main event to sell, Netflix is no longer interested. Perhaps Jake Paul’s MMA debut would qualify? There aren’t many other options that could generate that kind of buzz. This news does not mean that MVP will never hold another MMA event, as there are plenty of other streaming platforms and potential pay-per-view (PPV) options. It’s a definite blow to the promotion, however, as the Netflix partnership was a major advantage in helping MVP carve out space in the US MMA scene. It’s a little surprising as well, since the inaugural Rousey vs. Carano event produced such strong numbers . Help us, KI MMA, you’re our only hope?

item.title: Team player Harry Kane deserves Ballon d’Or says Bayern Munich coach
item.description: (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany did not hold back his support and admiration for Harry Kane to win the Ballon d’Or, praising the forward’s selfless contribution and consistency over the years. “Now that the voting is over, I don’t have to hide or be diplomatic. What made Harry happy the most in recent years is that he finally won his first team trophies here. Now if he can crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be deserved for the way he pl ays for the team,” said Kompany (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). In Wednesday’s game against Arsenal in the Champions League, Kane was the linchpin for Bayern. Miss ing key players in Michael Olise and Joshua Ki mmich, Bayern were in desperate need of a coordinator who could handle the physical pressure from the visitors. Harry Kane stepped in by stepping back and began orchestrating the Bayern attack. Of Kane’s 19 accurate passes, 6 of them were into the opposition’s final third. That is how often Kane pulle d back to collect and progress the ball into the attack. In comparison, Bayern’s starting midfielders had 7 passes each into the final third, while only Martin Ødegaard and left-back Riccardo Calafiori from Arsenal’s camp surpassed Kane in this stat. Time and again, Kane has proven that he can become what his team needs him to be. A makeshift tackler, defensive midfielder, box-to-box central midfielder, or attacking midfielder whose passes can split the opposition and create chances—Harry has done it all over the last two seasons. At Bayern, the 33-year-old has hit a new peak in his footballing ability that deserves the highest recognition in the sport. Join the conversation! item.title: Herb Dean Receives Sympathy From UFC Star Alex Pereira
item.description: Herb Dean Alex Pereira UFC Getty UFC star Alex Pereira expressed sympathy towards MMA referee Herb Dean, who has been getting booed routinely by fans at UFC events. Dean was heavily criticized by Pereira in the wake of his TKO loss to Ciryl Gane at UFC Freedom 250 in June, in a failed attempt to win the interim UFC heavyweight title. Since then, other fighters have spoken up about Dean’s inconsistent officiating, and now, when he is introduced as the ref at UFC events, the fans boo him. Pereira feels bad. Alex Pereira Feels Bad for Herb Dean Speaking on “The Ariel Helwani Show,” Pereira admitted that he feels bad for Dean now. “I see everything that’s going on, and sometimes I do feel bad because I know it’s his job, but when I spoke, I was just advocating because he’s the guy to be there who’s supposed to be protecting the fighters and avoid that something worse could happen to a fighter. I had to speak my mind. But yeah, I do feel bad for him sometimes, some certain ways,” Pereira said (via MMAjunkie.com ). Alex Pereira Doesn’t Want Herb Dean to Officiate His Fights While Pereira does have sympathy for what Dean has been going through, getting booed by the fans so much lately, he doesn’t want the veteran referee to officiate any of his fights going forward. “I don’t know how things role in the fight night, but if I can have a choice, I definitely don’t want him refereeing my fights no more,” Pereira said. While the athletic commissions ultimately make the final call on which referees will officiate the fights, they will take into consideration when a certain fighter believes that there is an issue with a referee, so it’s possible that Dean won’t ref Pereira’s fights anymore since there was clearly an issue between the two. Pereira, by the way, makes his long-awaited return to the Octagon at UFC 335 in December when he takes on Sergei Pavlovich in a heavyweight slugfest. If Pereira wins that fight, then he is expected to be the No. 1 contender and get a UFC heavyweight title shot. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Herb Dean Receives Sympathy From UFC Star Alex Pereira appeared first on HEAVY .

Shreyas Iyer leads the side with Tilak Varma as his deputy, while Mitchell Santner captains the hosts. One name is still waiting for a chance. Fans once again remain excited to know if 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will finally return to the fray for Team India. The left-hander last played for India in the Asian Games scoring 53 runs across two innings against Sri Lanka and Pakistan. It looks unlikely, although the final XI will only be confirmed at the toss. item.title: Robert Garcia Concerned About Canelo Card Safety in Saudi Arabia
item.description: What to Know With less than ten days to go, the October 31 card featuring Canelo Álvarez vs. Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is still scheduled to go ahead even as violent attacks continue and spread. Turki Alalshikh, Chairman of the General Entertainment Authority and President of the Saudi Boxing Federation, published next week’s Fight Week calendar. Trainer Robert Garcia said Wednesday he is worried about the safety of his fighter Lindolfo Delgado and his team, and has no travel arrangements in place yet. With less than ten days before the last Riyadh Season card of the year, “Mexico vs the World,” scheduled for October 31 in Riyadh, most fighters and their teams would have traveled to Saudi Arabia to acclimate to the time zone and climate and prepare for their bouts. But Riyadh Airport has been closed, and according to trainer Robert Garcia, who will work the corner of his welterweight challenger, Lindolfo Delgado of Mexico (24-0, 16 KOs) , who will fight for the vacant IBF title against Arthur Biyarslanov (21-0, 17 KOs), a stablemate of Christian Mbilli, his travel plans are (pardon the pun) still up in the air. Speaking on the subscription “ Boxing Scene Today ” show on Wednesday, Garcia said he believes the fight card will take place. But he is otherwise in the dark, a shocking development for a trainer whose fighter is expected to fight for his first world title in 10 days. Canelo vs Mbilli Card Still Scheduled Turki Alalshikh of the Saudi General Entertainment Authority posted the Mexico vs the World Fight Week schedule on Wednesday. Further cementing Garcia’s opinion is the social media accounts of Turki Alalshikh, chairman of the General Entertainment Authority, and RING Magazine. Both recently posted the full schedule of Fight Week Activities. It’s unclear who feels safe enough to move around and attend from a fan perspective. Fighters may appear in a closed venue and be streamed live worldwide. All events are scheduled for 2 p.m. ET/11 a.m. PT and will air on DAZN Boxing PPV . In addition, Alalshikh is still promoting online ticket sales, as recently as 12 hours before publication on Wednesday. Meanwhile, the U.S. ordered its embassy personnel to leave Saudi Arabia and directed all non-emergency government employees and their families to leave the country. There are murmurs about additional unconfirmed evacuations. Safety Concerns Continue to Worry Fight Teams “They’re already announcing the grand arrivals and all that all that nice information. But I still haven’t got no flights yet. I still have no flight information. They haven’t told me anything,” said Garcia. Conde Nast Traveler magazine, among the most respected travel news sources, reports it is not considered safe to travel to Saudi Arabia in an article on Tuesday . After being closed for more than a week, the King Khalid Airport in Riyadh resumed operations on Sunday, October 18. This does not mean a return to normal schedules. Flights must secure prior permission

After being closed for more than a week, the King Khalid Airport in Riyadh resumed operations on Sunday, October 18. This does not mean a return to normal schedules. Flights must secure prior permission from Saudi aviation authorities to land or take off. Dozens of international routes are still suspended. Attacks continue and are spreading. Saudi authorities have targeted attacks on airports in Abha, Jazan, Najran and Dammam, as well as Saudi Aramco oil facilities. This is cause for concern even if teams make travel arrangements that avoid major Saudi airports. “What I was told the last couple days was that we were flying to Dubai, (and) from Dubai to some small airport near where the fights are going to be and then drive like a four-hour drive to get there,” said Garcia. Athletes and their teams work hard to minimize anything that could throw them off their preparations and focus. Worrying about travel arrangements and personal safety doesn’t set anyone up for success. Robert Garcia: ‘Hell No!’ Robert Garcia wraps the hands of Lindolfo Delgado for a training session at the Robert Garcia Boxing Academy. Photo: Top Rank Boxing “Man, I don’t want to be in the documentary 25 years from now. You know, talking about all these brave fighters that went out there and coaches and managers and trainers that went out there and never came back. Hell no! I don’t want to. I don’t,” insisted Garcia. Despite his concerns, he is still making plans to accompany Lindolfo Delgado to Riyadh with a championship on the line, one he’s worked for his entire career. “As of now, my team, at least my team with Lindolfo Delgado, we’ve been waiting all weekend. We don’t have no flights. We don’t have no information. So honestly, I really don’t know what’s going to happen. Garcia said the decision boils down to Canelo Alvarez. Alvarez has apparently stood firm, insisting the card will continue. Garcia said if the undercard fighters decide to bow out at the end, he believes Alvarez, and his two stablemates Jaime Munguia and Rafael Espinosa who are all trained by Eddy Reynoso, and their opponents will be all that’s needed to make the card happen. “That’s all they need. That’s probably why they haven’t even told us about any flights or anything. We haven’t had no information.” Garcia will be in San Antonio this week to work the corner of his featherweight prospect Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez on the Navarrete vs Foster undercard, then make his way (in theory) to the Middle East. “I’m going to San Antonio, but at least Lindolfo and the rest of my team should have already known they’re flying out the next couple days to be there, at least one week before. We can’t be sitting waiting and thinking, ‘oh yeah, we’re just waiting for that flight. They’ll send it to us.’ They would have already. They should have already. Honestly, I don’t know. We don’t have flights yet,” said Garcia. How Serious Is The Threat? As I reported previously for NY Fights , the U.S. State Department and the governments of Canada and Mexico continues to warn citizens to avoid all non-essential travel to the region, including Saudi Arabia. The fight card is currently scheduled to take place in Riyadh on October 31. DAZN Boxing will broadcast it live starting at 12 noon ET/9 a.m. PT with prelim fights The U.S. State Department has active travel advisories in place for the Middle East, including a Level 3: Reconsider Travel advisory for Saudi Arabia, including conflict escalation, flight cancellations, and airspace closures. A Level 3 alert is labeled “Reconsider Travel” and covers Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Isreal, and the West Bank. Details here . The State Department cites active threats from Iranian drone and missile targeting along with attacks and threats from Houthi rebels in Yemen directed at Saudi territory, infrastructure, and American interests. Falling debris from intercepted projectiles also poses a danger. This is not the highest alert level. Level 4 is “Do Not Travel.” It’s far too late to move the card to another venue. It’s highly doubtful it will be postponed. Funding for cards in Riyadh is somewhat in doubt. October 31 is currently the last boxing card in Riyadh on the calendar. The main card stars, including the three Mexican A-side fighters Alvarez , Munguia, and Espinoza, and their immediate corner teams will receive VIP travel and, if necessary, military protection to enter the country safely. They need their opponents, so it would be surprising if they didn’t get security escorts. But the rest of the undercard, like Garcia’s fighter Lindolfo Delgado, may be on their own. It’s a tough call to turn down a title fight opportunity. Canelo Alvarez says he’ll go through hell to get his WBC championship belt back. Photo: DAZN Boxing On the Boxing Scene podcast, reporter Lance Pugmire said a member of the Alvarez team told him Canelo is determined to get his WBC belt back from Christian Mbilli. He also has to move forward with the fight to get paid. “He wants to fight,” reported Pugmire. “He has told some people close to him, ‘I am willing to go to hell to get my belt back.’ “And som

item.title: Diomande outshines booed Vinícius as Mbappé leads Real Madrid past Leipzig 4-1
item.description: Diomande outshines booed Vinícius as Mbappé leads Real Madrid past Leipzig 4-1 Real Madrid made it three wins from three in the Champions League as Kylian Mbappé scored and assisted in a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig at the Bernabéu. Substitute Yan Diomande also scored and assisted against his old club, days before a Clásico that the banned Vinícius Júnior will miss. Real Madrid kept their Champions League record perfect with victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday night. José Mourinho’s side have won all three league-phase games. They beat Inter 2-1 at home on matchday one and came from behind to win 4-3 at Roma on matchday two. Mbappé was the top-rated player on the night with 8.42. Yet the second half belonged just as much to Vinícius Júnior and the man who replaced him. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring just before half-time, in the 43rd minute. It was his first goal since joining the club. Madrid led 1-0 at the break. Güler doubled the lead from Mbappé’s pass after the restart. It was a second successive match with a goal for Güler. Diomande makes his mark against his old club Diomande came on for Vinícius in the 70th minute. Some Bernabéu fans whistled the Brazilian as he left the pitch, OKDIARIO reported. The substitute then laid on Mbappé’s goal. Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for Leipzig in the 85th minute, assisted by Christoph Baumgartner. Diomande restored the three-goal margin two minutes later from a Brahim Díaz pass. He left Leipzig in the summer in a deal that could be worth up to €140 million. His rating of 7.55 came from 20 minutes on the pitch. Mourinho said the change showed the strength of his bench rather than unhappiness with Vinícius. He added that Diomande or Endrick could change the pace of the game. The numbers backed Madrid’s control. They had 65% of the ball and 18 shots to Leipzig’s 11. Their expected goals reached 3.13 against 1.51. Thibaut Courtois still made five saves for a rating of 7.89. Leipzig have now lost two in a row, after a 1-6 defeat to Bayern München. Vinícius ban opens the door before the Clásico Vinícius cannot play at the Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday 25 October. He is serving his suspension after being sent off against Villarreal. LaLiga has scheduled the matchday-ten Clásico for 21:00. Madrid head to Barcelona on a run of four straight wins in all competitions. That sequence includes victories over Villarreal, Roma and Sevilla. Their last defeat was 1-2 against Atlético Madrid. The form of Diomande offers Mourinho one option in Vinícius’s absence. Leipzig return to the Bundesliga at home to SV Elversberg on Saturday 24 October. Madrid’s next Champions League fixture is away to AEK Athens on Wednesday 4 November, kicking off at 18:45 CET. item.title: Angel Reese’s confidence is overflowing in powerful message after Dream’s Game 3 win
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Angel Reese’s confidence is overflowing in powerful message after Dream’s Game 3 win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . ATLANTA – Sometimes, it’s just about who wants it more. After letting Game 1 slip through their hands, the Atlanta Dream have responded in the best way possible, and it’s started with Angel Reese herself. In Game 2, her relentlessness and determination to will the team to a victory worked. Whatever high she was on from that game carried over to Atlanta, and it once again helped the Dream to a 97-71 win against the Golden State Valkyries to put them up 2-1 in the series. At this point, it feels like the Dream go when Reese goes, and that’s no problem for her since she sees what it does for them. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “No matter if my shots are falling, I just want to make sure I bring energy,” Reese said after the game. “I just want to be able to come in every day, pour into everybody, bring the energy, bring the morale, because I think it’s contagious. “When you have a mentality that, starting for me, I’m hyped all the time, and I bring the confidence to everyone, y’all not taking this from us. And that’s in my heart. I’m not letting you take this from us, and it becomes contagious within the team. They feel that confidence too. That’s kind of been my mindset throughout the entire season, just being able to want it more than anybody else.” There’s no doubt that the Dream felt it, and it all started in the first quarter. As much as Reese set the tone, she had help from Naz Hillmon, who hit back-to-back 3-pointers in the first. “I think our 3s were huge,” Hillmon said. “Very timely. But I think it also helped to open up our teammates. We’re knocking them down; you can’t continue to help into the paint, bring two to Angel, Rhyne [Howard] or Lish [Gray]. Definitely opened up things that we’ve been working on all year long, and it was nice to see them fall tonight.” Though the Dream were up as much as 12 points in the second quarter, the Valkyries made their run. Janelle Salaün gave them a boost with 12 points, and they were able to outscore the Dream 25-23 in the quarter. Still, it was the home team that had the momentum and went into halftime with a six-point lead. item.title: Moises Caicedo vs Claude Makelele: Why Chelsea comparison makes sense as Gus Poyet explains the value of an ‘old-fashioned’ No.6 in a Premier League title-winning team
item.description: Claude Makelele Moises Caicedo Chelsea - Getty/GOAL Makelele starred for Mourinho's Blues Back in 2003, when Roman Abramovich was financing an ambitious project in west London, France international Makelele was lured away from La Liga giants Real Madrid. He was considered to form part of the global elite . The arrival of Jose Mourinho as Chelsea manager a year later revolutionised the Blues, with the ‘Special One’ assembling a squad that was virtually untouchable across his debut campaign. Just 15 goals were conceded in the 2004-05 Premier League season. Makelele helped to deliver domestic dominance, with opposition attacks often being snuffed out before the likes of John Terry and Petr Cech were called into attack. The value of a match-altering No.6 has continued to grow since then. In the present, Caicedo is charged with carrying out those duties in the English capital. He was acquired in 2023 as part of a £100 million ($134m) transfer agreement with Brighton . Injuries have held him back at times of late, but full fitness appears to have been recaptured. Can Caicedo be compared with Makelele? Can Caicedo be compared with Makelele? Many have been quick to suggest that the South American has reached Makelele-esque performance levels . Asked if he shares that opinion, former Blues midfielder Poyet - who was speaking in association with Gambling.com, the go-to source for casino sites - told GOAL : “Makelele, his trajectory, his career was incredible. I think he [Caicedo] needs to keep performing at this level for a few years to be able to compare. “I think it's too early, but at the same time, he's so important for this team. It's unbelievable the difference between the first four or five games without Caicedo to the last two with Caicedo. And that shows how much they were missing him, especially in this system that he's trying to play Xabi [Alonso], to allow the three up front to go on and produce. “I think also that with all respect to Caicedo, the help of [Jordan] Henderson next to him not too many people were expecting, also giving him the chance to be himself. So I think he's a key player this season for Chelsea and I really hope that he keeps himself fit.” Kante another title winner at Stamford Bridge Makelele is not the only formidable Frenchman to have helped Chelsea to the Premier League crown. In 2016-17, having already formed part of Leicester’s odd-busting title triumph, N’Golo Kante enhanced his reputation when excelling for Antonio Conte’s Blues. Could Caicedo follow that trophy-winning trend, having already savoured Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup successes? Poyet added when that question was put to him: “I was there in the game against Bournemouth and when you see the fluidity of the team going forward, everybody wants to score and you need someone who, tactically, sometimes people don't see where he's standing, where he's looking, where he's pointing to, where he's covering, like reading the game. “And those are the spec

And that shows how much they were missing him, especially in this system that he's trying to play Xabi [Alonso], to allow the three up front to go on and produce. “I think also that with all respect to Caicedo, the help of [Jordan] Henderson next to him not too many people were expecting, also giving him the chance to be himself. Poyet added when that question was put to him: “I was there in the game against Bournemouth and when you see the fluidity of the team going forward, everybody wants to score and you need someone who, tactically, sometimes people don't see where he's standing, where he's looking, where he's pointing to, where he's covering, like reading the game. “And those are the special players that you named. Makelele, because of his ability to be ahead of the game. N’Golo Kante, because I never see somebody running that much in my life. I have seen players running, but he covered the whole pitch. “I think it shows that we still need that player, number six, proper, old-fashioned, staying in front of the back four in every single team in the world. That sometimes with this new mentality of passing, passing, passing and Barcelona style or [Pep] Guardiola style or Spanish style, we forget about that central midfielder.” Chelsea continue to spend big on transfers Chelsea continue to spend big on transfers Caicedo’s value is not lost on anybody at Stamford Bridge, with the all-action 24-year-old - who has taken on captaincy duties in certain fixtures - becoming one of the first names on the team sheet. Chelsea have continued to spend big on more pieces of a title-chasing puzzle that are being slotted together around their No.25, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro and Emi Martinez hoping to help the Blues back to the summit of English and European football .

item.title: Manchester United humiliated 4-1 by Como as Tielemans says “everything was missing”
item.description: Manchester United humiliated 4-1 by Como as Tielemans says “everything was missing” Youri Tielemans admitted there were no positives to take from Manchester United 's 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. Manchester United were thrashed by the tournament debutants on a disastrous night in Italy, with Nico Paz starring for the Serie A side with two goals and an assist. The result continued a wretched run for Michael Carrick's team, who have lost two of their opening three games in Europe. Their poor form has now stretched to seven consecutive games without a win in all competitions, their longest run in over a decade, since an eight-match winless run between November and December 2015. Tielemans said that 'everything was missing' during a disappointing night at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. The Belgian called on Manchester United to bounce back quickly, ahead of Sunday's visit from Bournemouth in the Premier League. “We played very poor and conceded after two minutes and then it puts you on the back foot straight away," the midfielder said to MUTV. “We want to be positive and go forward but this wasn’t the way. “There was more said at half-time about us trying to get back into the game, but they score just after half-time, so it wasn’t a great atmosphere in the changing rooms. “We need to move on as we have games coming. Everything was missing tonight. We were disjointed as a team, we didn’t play well together, our press was off and when we were on the ball, we could not make the right decisions, so you get frustrated with the game. “They [Como] played around us too easily, it was a poor night.” Carrick apologies to fans as Man Utd thrashed by Como Michael Carrick added that the performance was 'nowhere near good enough' from his team and apologised to the supporters that had made the trip. He insisted he cares about the club 'as much as anybody' as he battles to turn results around. “It was nowhere near good enough in so many ways. We didn't deserve to get anything from the game. We actually started and had a chance with Diogo [Dalot] and created that, and then pretty much after that, we didn't do enough in the game. In terms of individually, collectively, we just weren't there. "We wanted to build on Leeds and we did pretty much the complete opposite. So, I just apologise to the supporters. I went over at the end to apologise because they pay so much and they care so much. I care about this club as much as anybody. I found it hard watching that tonight, I have to say, so I feel for them tonight, especially.”

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

The manager was delighted with the fight that his players showed, Declan Rice earning a deserved point with an 82nd-minute equaliser. Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. The Bayern striker set up Alphonso Davies for 1-1 before giving his team the lead from the penalty spot. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...
